systems.title: Core combat loop and wave/depth progression
systems.summary: In play this is a fully automatic, zero-input wave treadmill: one champion fights an identical enemy sprite over and over in a fixed arena, every 5th wave is that region's boss, each cleared wave instantly pays gleam (+cores/chest on bosses), and when the champion dies it respawns at full HP and restarts from wave 1 with nothing lost. The player never touches the fight — the ONLY interactive element on the combat screen is a 4-button BATTLE SPEED selector (x1/x2/x4/x8) (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:866-877`); everything else is decided in other screens (Build/Mastery/Stats/Gear/Map) and read passively here. The fight itself resolves instantly in one call (`SoloExpedition.PushWave`) and is then *replayed* as animation; reward crediting is gated on that animation finishing, so the speed button is a real ~2x throughput lever, not cosmetic. Run length is decided almost entirely by HP attrition against a compounding enemy-damage curve, and because the boss's 2.2x scale is applied to enemy DAMAGE as well as health (`SoloExpedition.cs:136`), 20 of 21 simulated runs across the whole training range end on a boss wave — depth is quantized to multiples of 5 and long stretches of stat investment produce literally zero depth change. Design intent and code have fully diverged: `combat-encounter-system.md` (1303 lines: weak-point targeting, dodge/block/interrupt, Resonance meter, ultimates) and `expedition-auto-battle.md` (5-creature squad, bank-or-push priced exit) describe systems with zero implementation in `src/`.
playerActions: Click one of four BATTLE SPEED buttons — x1/x2/x4/x8 (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:66`, click handler `:876`). This is the ONLY clickable thing on the combat screen. 'AUTO HUNT' next to it is a static painted label, not a toggle (`:879-883`). At starter power this swings real-world gleam/sec by roughly 2x (per-wave animation overhead — 0.8s break `:67` + ~0.4s enemy slide-in `:238,347` — is NOT sped up, so x8 only compresses the combat portion).

Weave 4 skills, each an independent (Source, Form, Vow) triple, in the Build screen (B). Source is a free cycle with no cost (`PlayerLoadout.cs:56-60`), so picking a Source strong against the fixed region theme is a free +50% (`ResonanceWeaving.cs:112,148-161`) — there is exactly one correct answer per region and it never changes.
Socket up to 3 of 13 keystones (`Build.cs:223`, `Keystones.cs:29-124`) — but only those the Memory Dust tree has taught.

Allocate mastery-tree points (43 nodes: 1 start + 24 arm minors + 6 bridges + 6 notables + 6 masteries; `MasteryTree.cs:66-121`). Only the 6 notables (grant a trigger) and the 6 mastery corners (set the affinity multiplier) change how combat resolves; the other 31 are flat +6%..+18% stat nodes. Respec is free and instant (`MasteryTree.cs:226-230`).
Spend gleam on 9 trainable stats in the Stats screen (V), rank cost 25 x 1.05^rank, cap 60 (`HunterProgression.cs:17-19`).
Equip gear in the Character screen (C) — 8 slots; weapon/charm/focus drive damage/health/skill-rate, Rare+ items carry one of 11 enchantment triggers.
Travel to another region on the Map (W). Changing region resets `Deepest` to 0 and restarts the run from wave 1 (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:248-252`).
NOT available in the fight: no targeting, no ability trigger, no retreat, no bank, no pause, no positioning, no reaction to the enemy windup (the windup outline `:548-552` is decoration).
numbers: Wave threat compounds: `EnemyScaleBase = 1.06^wave` — `src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Expeditions/WaveModel.cs:17`, applied at `:80`.
Wave reward is linear: `HaulScaleSlope = 0.35` → `haulScale = 1 + 0.35*wave` — `WaveModel.cs:20`, `:100`.

Boss every 5 waves, `BossHealthScale = 2.2` — `WaveModel.cs:23,26`. CRITICAL: `SoloExpedition.cs:136` multiplies `_enemyBaseDamage` by the same `scale`, so a boss also hits **2.2x harder**. The doc comment at `WaveModel.cs:25` only claims health. This is what actually ends runs.

Tick ceiling 120,000ms at 100ms/tick — `WaveModel.cs:29-30`. A wave that can't be killed inside it is `Stalled` and pays nothing (`SoloBattle.cs:389`); unreachable in practice, runs die of attrition long first.

Enemy base health = `110 * (1 + 0.35*regionProgression) * (1 + 0.35*regionIndex) * corruptionScale * regionModifier` — `Game1.cs:1228`. Enemy base damage = `9 * (1 + 0.20*regionProgression) * (1 + 0.25*regionIndex) * corruptionScale * regionModifier` — `Game1.cs:1229`.

`regionProgression` = 0/2/3/4, derived from region mastery which accrues +5 RMP per cleared wave with thresholds at 500/2000/5000 (`Game1.cs:1030`, `RegionAutomation.cs:11-15,186`). Farming a region ~100 waves makes its enemies +70% HP / +40% damage with no combat-side compensation — only a +N loot-tier bump (`Game1.cs:1302`).

Enemy bite interval 1500ms baseline; region AttackBias bends it to Heavy 2200ms / Fast 1000ms with an exactly compensating damage multiplier (2200/1500, 1000/1500) — `SoloExpedition.cs:45,60-65`. Net DPS identical; only TRAP proc frequency and spike size change. Verified: Verdant (Balanced) and Cinderworks (Heavy) both reach depth 19 at starter power.
Form base damage: Strike 45, Projectile 38, Aura 22, Trap 55, Mark 0, Transformation 30 — `ResonanceWeaving.cs:115-123`. Scaled by `1 + 0.008 * ResonanceAffinity` (`:110,203`).

Form cooldowns: Strike 2000, Projectile 900, Aura 0/passive, Trap 3000, Mark 4000, Transformation 2500 ms — `FormBehaviour.cs:45-53`. Aura ticks every 500ms (`:59`), Mark window 2500ms at 1.6x (`:68,76`), Transformation leeches 50% (`:79`).
Auto-attack: 6 damage every 1200ms — `SoloBattle.cs:52-53`. At starter power that is ~4% of total DPS; it exists only to prevent a stall.
Affinity (Nen hexagon): cyclic distance 0 → 2.00x, 1 → 1.15x, 2 → 0.75x, 3 → 0.45x — `FormBehaviour.cs:110-116`. Applies only if a mastery corner is taken.
Source matchup: circulant 6x6, strong 1.5x / weak 0.667x — `ResonanceWeaving.cs:112-113,148-161`.

Crit is deterministic expected value, no RNG: `critFactor = 1 + clamp(crit%/100, 0, 0.75) * (1.5 + 0.01*Focus - 1)` — `SoloBattle.cs:86-89,156-160`. At base (5% crit, 10 Focus) that is a 1.03x factor on skill hits only. Defense: `100/(100+Defense)`, base Defense 0 → 1.0 — `SoloBattle.cs:92,161`; `HunterProgression.cs:46`.

Stat wiring: damage = `weaponMult * (1 + 0.010*AttackPower) * gearDamage`; health = `(1 + 0.012*Vitality) * charm * gear`; skillRate = `focusItem * gear * (1 + 0.006*Engineering)`; haul = `(1 + 0.010*Guile) * gear` — `HunterProgression.cs:233,237-238,263,269`.

Champion HP = `max(60, hunter.MaxHealth) * VowHealthMultiplier` (base 100), minted fresh at full every restart — `SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:276`, `HunterProgression.cs:45,145`. No between-wave regen except Transformation leech.
Payout per cleared wave: `Gleam = round(8 * haulScale * haulMult)`; `Cores = boss ? round(2*haulMult) : 0` — `SoloExpedition.cs:186,190`. Materials `1 + wave/20` per wave — `Game1.cs:1252`.
Conquest at depth 7 — `Game1.cs:1318`, duplicated as `ConquerAt = 7` in `SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:675`. Pays 40 Memory Dust x corruption multiplier — `Game1.cs:1280`.
Mastery points = `3 + deepestEver/5 + conqueredRegions*5 + warrenPool` — `Game1.cs:1274`.

Boss chest drop chance = `min(0.60, 0.30 + 0.015*lootTier)` — `Chest.cs:100-102,141-145`; `lootTier = 1 + regionIndex + regionProgression + wave/5 + corruptionTier + regionLootBonus` — `Game1.cs:1302-1304`.

Corruption ratchet: +60% enemy health per tier, +1 loot tier, rewards x(1+tier), 60*tier dust on deepening — `CorruptionScaling.cs:18-19,22,25-26,32-33`. Unlocked only after all 6 regions conquered (`Regions.cs:198-211`).

Region modifiers: Verdant +10% HP; Cinderworks +20% HP, +1 loot; Umbral +20% dmg, +1 loot; Marrow +25% HP/+10% dmg, +1; Still Archive +25% dmg, +2; Pale Choir +20% HP & dmg, +2 — `RegionModifiers.cs:25-30`.

MEASURED (Python re-implementation of `SoloBattle.ResolveWave`): starter build + untrained hunter reaches depth 19 in Verdant Hollow (~35s of sim combat, 894 gleam/run). Same build reaches depth 4 in Umbral Reach, depth 2 in Still Archive. Training ALL 9 stats to rank 30 reaches depth 49; rank 60 (the cap, ~79,560 total gleam per `HunterProgression.cs:324-328`) reaches depth 69. Depth changes only in steps of 5 — ranks 21/24/27 all give depth 44; ranks 45/48/51 all give depth 64.

MEASURED: 20 of 21 sampled runs across the full training range died on a boss wave (waves 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70). Depth is effectively 'how many boss walls did I clear', not a continuous curve.

MEASURED: at starter power, damage output barely matters — 4x Projectile, 3x Projectile+Mark, 2 Projectile/1 Strike/1 Transformation, 4x Transformation and the starter build ALL reach exactly depth 19, because the binding constraint is the 100 HP pool, not kill speed. Only builds slow enough to eat extra bites fall behind (4x Strike → depth 8).
systems.unlocks: Gated by nothing — the run auto-starts on boot (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:258`) and keeps fighting on every screen and while minimised (`Game1.cs:1026-1033`); region choice is gated by `World.IsUnlocked` (prereq region conquered, `Regions.cs:169-175`). It gates essentially everything else: gleam (the only stat-training currency), cores (Warren hatchlings), materials, boss chests (the sole item source), region unlocks at depth 7, mastery points (`3 + deepestEver/5 + conquered*5`), 40 Memory Dust per conquest, and the corruption endgame (all 6 regions conquered).
systems.depth: Effectively zero in the moment and shallow out of it: the only in-fight input is a speed button, and off-fight the build space collapses because ~31 of 43 mastery nodes, 15 of 44 dust nodes, and 5 of 13 keystones are flat multipliers, the Source pick has one correct answer per region, VOW OF PATIENCE is a free 1.6x after 10 seconds, and the whole Rarity channel is disconnected.
gaps: `BuildMods.Rarity` → `Haul.Quality` is computed (`SoloExpedition.cs:191`) and NEVER read. `Game1.cs:1238-1252` consumes only `Haul.Gleam` and `Haul.Cores`. Chest loot quality comes from the chest's own rarity (`Chest.cs:184,192`), not the build. Consequence: FORTUNE (Rarity x2, damage x0.75) and DISCERNING EYE (Rarity x2, haul x0.5) are strictly negative keystones; the `fortune_1/fortune_2/ks_fortune` dust road (105 dust) buys nothing.

SPLINTER is dead the same way — `SoloBattle.cs:188` adds +0.15 quality per kill into the same discarded channel. REAPER (grants Splinter, costs -25% skill rate) is therefore a pure downside. `TriggerLivenessTests.cs:295` asserts only that the number lands in the bonus object, not that it reaches loot.

AURA completely ignores `mods.SkillRate` — its tick gate is `ms % AuraTickMs` with no rate divisor (`SoloBattle.cs:274-279`). Consequence: TITAN (Health x3, SkillRate x0.4) is a cost-free x3 health upgrade for an Aura build. MEASURED: 4x Aura goes 14 → 19 depth with TITAN, while 4x Projectile goes 19 → 14 with the same keystone.

BLOODLUST and ZEAL stack multiplicatively (`SoloBattle.cs:207-221`). Taking the Bloodlust keystone (or the free `strike_n` mastery notable, `MasteryTree.cs:83`) together with JUGGERNAUT guarantees a minimum 1.8x damage at any health fraction (1.96x at 50%). JUGGERNAUT carries `BuildMods.None` — its only cost is NoHealing (`Keystones.cs:103-106`).

VOW OF PATIENCE (`ResonanceWeaving.cs:282-287`) triggers on expedition-ABSOLUTE elapsed ms ≥ 10,000, which is monotonic across waves — so it latches permanently on from ~wave 7 and pays 1.6x for free. It strictly dominates VOW OF THE UNBROKEN (same 1.6x, conditional on HP) and out-earns both static-cost vows (1.333x and 1.45x, both with real costs). It is also the FIRST vow the dust tree teaches (`vow_study_1`, 15 dust).

The boss's 2.2x is applied to enemy DAMAGE as well as health (`SoloExpedition.cs:136` passes the same `scale` to both parameters). Undocumented — `WaveModel.cs:25` says 'a boss's health on top of the wave's own scaling'. This single line is what quantizes all progression to 5-wave steps.

The floating combat numbers are FABRICATED. `SpawnDamage` is fed `HitDamage(mult)` = `PowerRating * mult * jitter` (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:330-335,369,381`), not `e.Amount` from the `BattleEvent`, even though the sim puts real damage in `Amount` (`SoloBattle.cs:236`). Crits shown on screen are `form == Form.Trap`, not real crits. The enemy health bar (driven by `WaveReplay` from real `Amount`s) and the damage numbers disagree by construction.

The whole encounter-authoring layer is dead code relative to combat. `EncounterTemplate`, `CreatureTemplate`, `PowerTierBase`, `SelectionWeight`, `CreaturePool`, `ParClearTimeSeconds`, `EncounterSpawner` (`Encounters/`) are referenced only inside `Encounters/` — consumed by `World.FarmParSeconds` for the idle farm. The fight reads two floats computed in `Game1.cs:1228-1229`. Per-region boss HP values (3200/6000/10000/15000/24000, `Regions.cs:47-68`) reach nothing.

Design docs describe a different game. `design/gdd/combat-encounter-system.md` (1303 lines) specifies manual weak-point targeting, dodge charges, block, interrupt, a Resonance meter and an ultimate — grep finds zero implementations in `src/`. `design/gdd/expedition-auto-battle.md` specifies a 5-creature squad and a bank-vs-push priced exit (100%/60%/30%); the code has one champion and pays every wave immediately (`SoloExpedition.cs:194-198`).

Region combat bias is presentationally real but mechanically neutral: `BiasTempo` (`SoloExpedition.cs:60-65`) compensates the damage exactly for the interval change, so Heavy/Fast/Balanced deliver identical DPS. Its only live effect is TRAP proc count. Verified by simulation (Verdant/Balanced and Cinderworks/Heavy both hit depth 19 at starter power).

No death penalty exists. Rewards are paid per wave, and a wipe mints a brand-new full-health champion (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:272-282`). The stated 'push or hold' tension in the code comments has no mechanism behind it — there is nothing to hold.

`_regionProgression` makes a region strictly harder as you farm it (+35% HP / +20% damage per level) with no offsetting combat benefit, only a loot-tier bump. Combined with the 5-wave quantization, sustained farming can visibly LOSE the player a boss wall.

`Stalled` (`WaveOutcome.Stalled`, `SoloBattle.cs:389`) is authored, wired, and unreachable in practice — attrition kills the champion tens of waves before enemy health outruns DPS. All measured runs ended `Wiped`.
`ConquerWaveDepth = 7` is hardcoded twice (`Game1.cs:1318` and `SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:675` with a comment acknowledging the duplication).
`_speedMul` (the one real player lever) is not persisted — it resets to x2 on every launch (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:64-65`).

Only one boss has authored render metadata: `BossMetaFor` contains `crystal_lich` only (`SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:86-93`); the other five regions' bosses fall back to `DefaultBossMeta`. Visual variety per region is exactly one trash sprite (keyed off the region's Source, `:103-107`) plus one boss.

systems.title: Hunter levelling, stats, training and power
systems.summary: Hunter levelling/stats/training is a fully-built system with no reachable entry point. The nine-stat catalog (`HunterProgression.cs:9-13`), the geometric Gleam training curve, the 60-rank cap, the save round-trip and ~12 unit tests all exist and work — but the only method that writes a rank, `Hunter.Train()` (`HunterProgression.cs:284`), is called from exactly three places: two `RH_SHOT_MODE` screenshot fixtures (`Game1.cs:761-762,772-775`) and save-restore (`SaveGame.cs:447`). The STATS screen that used to own training was rebuilt read-only on 2026-07-28 (`StatsScreen.cs:60` — `Update()` is an empty body; commit `c4319bd` says so in its own message: "stat TRAINING (hunter.Train) is no longer reachable — flagged for the owner"). Consequence for the live player: all nine stats are permanently frozen at their base values, HUNTER LEVEL is permanently 1 (`HunterProgression.cs:106` — level is `1 + totalRanks/5`, and totalRanks is always 0), and the nav legend still advertises "STATS — TRAIN" (`Game1.cs:1783`). What the player actually experiences under the "hunter power" label is a gear-only curve: `PowerRating` (`Gear.cs:113-114`) is a 3-term arithmetic sum that reads the weapon multiplier, the charm, and Defense affixes — and ignores every trait, every Damage/Health/SkillRate/Haul/Crit affix, and six of the eight equipment slots.
playerActions: Nothing. There is no decision in this system as shipped — the STATS screen's Update() is `{ }` (`StatsScreen.cs:60`) and no other screen calls Train/CanTrain/NextRankCost (verified: zero non-test, non-fixture call sites).
Press V to read a five-panel read-only stat sheet (`StatsScreen.cs:63-77`). Every number on it is a constant for the life of the save except the four rows that gear moves.
Equip/unequip gear on the GEAR screen (`CharacterScreen.cs:140-164`) — the only input in the game that changes any value this system displays.

Click EQUIP BEST (`CharacterScreen.cs:163,177-187`), which auto-sorts by `PowerContribution`. Because PowerRating ignores traits and 5 of 6 affix types, for Helm/Chest/Gloves/Boots/Ring/Focus this ranks purely on Defense-affix magnitude and treats a 4-affix Legendary with no Defense roll as worth exactly 0.
numbers: Stat catalog: 9 stats — AttackPower, Focus, Vitality, Engineering, Guile, ResonanceAffinity, MaxHealth, Defense, CriticalChance (`src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Economy/HunterProgression.cs:9-13`)

Training cost: `round(25 × 1.05^n)` — BaseTrainingCost 25, TrainingGrowthRate 1.05, StatRankCap 60 (`HunterProgression.cs:17-19`, formula at `:275-278`). Rank 1 = 25g, rank 60 = 445g. Full lifetime sink = 9 × 8,840 = 79,556 Gleam (`HunterProgression.cs:324-328`).
Gain per rank: +2.0 for the six core stats, +5.0 MaxHealth, +2.0 Defense, +0.25 CriticalChance (percentage points) (`HunterProgression.cs:25-33`)

Base values (the values the live game is permanently pinned to): AttackPower 10, Focus 10, Vitality 10, Engineering 10, Guile 10, ResonanceAffinity 10, MaxHealth 100, Defense 0, CriticalChance 5 (`HunterProgression.cs:39-47`)

Hunter level: `1 + sum(ranks)/5` (`HunterProgression.cs:106`). Live value: always 1. Theoretical max 109 (540 ranks / 5 + 1). Drawn on 4 screens: `StatsScreen.cs:90,188`, `CharacterScreen.cs:222`, `BuildScreen.cs:223`, `SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:703`.

SquadDamageMultiplier = `GearDamageMultiplier × (1 + 0.010 × AttackPower) × WornMods.Damage` (`HunterProgression.cs:233`). Stat term is frozen at 1.10; maxed it would be 2.30 (a 2.09× swing the whole training curve buys).

SquadHealthMultiplier = `(1 + 0.012 × Vitality) × CharmToughness × WornMods.Health` (`HunterProgression.cs:237-238`). Stat term frozen at 1.12. CharmToughness = `1 + 0.06 × RarityPower × ItemLevelFactor` (`:251`).

SquadSkillRate = `FocusAttunement × WornMods.SkillRate × (1 + 0.006 × Engineering)` (`HunterProgression.cs:263`). Stat term frozen at 1.06. FocusAttunement = `1 + 0.05 × RarityPower × ItemLevelFactor` (`:266`).
HaulMultiplier = `(1 + 0.010 × Guile) × WornMods.Haul` (`HunterProgression.cs:269`). Stat term frozen at 1.10.

Skill base damage = `FormBaseValue × (1 + 0.008 × ResonanceAffinity)` (`ResonanceWeaving.cs:202-203`, coefficient at `:110`). Frozen at ×1.08. FormBaseValue: Strike 45, Projectile 38, Aura 22, Trap 55, Mark 0, Transformation 30 (`ResonanceWeaving.cs:115-123`).

Crit: `critFactor = 1 + clamp(CritChance+affixes, 0, 0.75) × (critMult − 1)`, `critMult = 1.5 + 0.01 × Focus` (`SoloBattle.cs:86,89,156-160`). Frozen at 5% chance × 1.60 mult = a flat +3% expected skill damage, forever. Maxed it would be 20% × 2.80.

Defense mitigation: `100 / (100 + Defense)` (`SoloBattle.cs:92,161`). Frozen at Defense 0 → 1.000 → 0% mitigation from the stat. Maxed rank-60 Defense = 120 → 54.5% reduction. All live mitigation comes from `CharmDefenseBonus = round(RarityPower × 12 × ItemLevelFactor)` (`Gear.cs:99`) plus Defense affixes at 8 base (`ItemAffixes.cs:54`).

Damage taken = `enemyDamage / max(0.05, mods.Health) × defenseFactor × fragilityMult` (`SoloBattle.cs:344`) — note Health is a divisor on damage taken, not a pool, so Vitality and MaxHealth are two unrelated toughness math paths.

PowerRating = `round(damageMult × attackPower × 2 + defense × 2 + maxHealth × 0.5)` (`Gear.cs:113-114`, exposed at `HunterProgression.cs:148`). Bare hunter = `1×10×2 + 0 + 50` = **70**. Fully-geared ceiling ≈ 745 (Legendary iL60 weapon → mult 12.96; Legendary iL60 charm → +143 Def, +299 HP).

Weapon multiplier = `1 + RarityPower × ItemLevelFactor` (`Gear.cs:95`); RarityPower 0.20/0.50/1.20/3.00/7.00 (`Gear.cs:69-77`); ItemLevelFactor = `1 + (iL−1) × 0.012` (`Gear.cs:91`, ×1.708 at iL60). Range 1.0 → 12.96.
Affinity multiplier: ×2.00 on-Form, ×1.15 adjacent, ×0.75 off, ×0.45 opposite (`FormBehaviour.cs:110-116`) — a 4.4× spread, the largest single lever in the fight and it costs nothing.

Mastery tree (the live substitute progression): 43 nodes = 1 start + 6 arms × 6 + 6 bridges (`MasteryTree.cs:70-121`). **36 are flat +6%..+18% Damage/Health/SkillRate/Haul; 6 (the notables) grant a BuildTrigger that changes how combat resolves; 1 is inert.** Points earned = `3 + deepestWave/5 + conquered×5 + warrenMasteryPool` (`Game1.cs:1274`).

Remaining Gleam sinks after training died: Refine `15 + iLvl × 8` gold + `4 + iLvl` scrap (`Forge.cs:218-219`), Greater Refine ×3 gold (`:231`), Warren facility upgrades `round(5300 × 1.5^level)` (`Warren.cs:64-65,133`).
Tuning is not data-driven: `ProgressionTuning.Default` is the only instance ever constructed (`Game1.cs:100` — `new Hunter()` with no argument), so every value above is a compile-time constant in C#.
systems.unlocks: Nothing gates it and it gates nothing: HunterLevel is explicitly cosmetic ("never a gate", `HunterProgression.cs:105`), region access is gated on conquering 7 waves rather than on any stat, and `MapScreen.HunterPower` is host-set every frame (`Game1.cs:1726`) but never read by any draw call (`MapScreen.cs:49` is its only other occurrence) — so the one place power could have gated content shows region PWR (`bossTier × 350`, `MapScreen.cs:84`) with nothing to compare it against.
systems.depth: Zero — there is no reachable choice; the nine stats are read-only constants and the only progression the player can act on is which item goes in which of eight slots.
gaps: TRAINING IS UNREACHABLE. `Hunter.Train()` has no player-facing caller. `StatsScreen.Update()` is an empty method body (`StatsScreen.cs:60`), and the class doc admits it: "stat TRAINING (hunter.Train) is intentionally not here — flagged for the owner, since it currently has no other home" (`StatsScreen.cs:22-23`). Commit `c4319bd` deleted the working train UI (rows with `TrainBtn`, `TryTrain`, "RANK n / 60", "NEXT RANK COSTS n GLEAM", and a live DPS bench) to conform to a UX spec that said the screen should be read-only.
Because of the above, ALL NINE STATS ARE FROZEN and HUNTER LEVEL IS PERMANENTLY 1 in normal play, while four screens display it as if it moves.

The nav legend still reads `("V", "STATS — TRAIN")` (`Game1.cs:1783`) and the keybind comment still reads "Commander training, spelled out, on its own page" (`Game1.cs:1024`). Both advertise a feature that no longer exists.

`DamageBench` (`Builds/DamageBench.cs`) — a live-sim DPS bench explicitly built "so a stat that quietly reaches no formula shows up plainly as 'trained it, the number did not budge'" — has zero call sites outside tests. The instrument built to detect this exact bug class was removed from the UI in the same commit that caused it.

~12 unit tests (`HunterStatWiringTests.cs`, `LootSystemTests.cs:161-190,242-272`, `DamageBenchTests.cs:59`, `SaveSystemTests.cs:20-21`, `FullLoopTests.cs:64-65`) all call `Train()` and all pass. The suite guards a system the player cannot touch, so CI is green on a dead feature.

79,556 Gleam of designed sink (`HunterProgression.cs:324-328`) was deleted from the economy without replacement. The GDD's entire §4.5 proof ("8.2–21.2 hours to absorb the sink") is void; remaining Gleam sinks are Refine and Warren upgrades only.

PowerRating is structurally blind to most of the item system: it reads only the weapon multiplier, the charm's Def/HP, and Defense affixes. It never reads `WornMods` (every GearTrait — HEAVY, SWIFT, WILD etc., `GearTraits.cs:114-135`) or the Damage/Health/SkillRate/Haul/Crit affixes (`ItemAffixes.cs:47-55`). Helm/Chest/Gloves/Boots/Ring/Focus contribute to it ONLY via a Defense affix, which is a 1-in-6 uniform roll (`ItemAffixes.cs:84`).

Consequence of the above: `PowerContribution` (`HunterProgression.cs:162-172`) is documented as the honest comparison basis, and it is self-consistent with PowerRating — but both are wrong about the fight. EQUIP BEST (`CharacterScreen.cs:177-187`) and the green ▲ upgrade badge (`CharacterScreen.cs:339`) therefore rank six of eight slots almost at random, and will actively downgrade a player who trusts them.

GDD vs code divergence in `design/gdd/hunter-progression-system.md` §3.4/§4.2/§4.4 — every single number differs. Doc: yields +1.0 (six stats), +10 MaxHealth, +0.005 crit; starting values 0 for eight stats. Code: +2.0, +5.0, +0.25pp; starting values 10/10/10/10/10/10/100/0/5. Doc: `hunter_level_ranks_per_level = 10`, max level 55. Code: /5, max level 109. Doc §3.3 mandates encounter-state gating on purchases; no such gate exists in `Hunter.Train`.

`design/gdd/progression.md` (the v1.0 release curve doc) does not mention training, stats, or hunter level at all — its §5 currency table lists Gleam's sinks as "gear Refine, facility upgrades" only. The release doc has already silently absorbed the loss without flagging it.
`MapScreen.HunterPower` is a write-only property — set at `Game1.cs:1726`, never read.

Gameplay values are hardcoded in C# records, not external config, contradicting `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md` ("Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded"). `ProgressionTuning`, `WeavingTuning`, `ForgeTuning`, `WarrenTuning` all ship as compile-time `Default` singletons.

systems.title: Skills / builds: Source x Form x Vow weaving and the mastery tree
systems.summary: A "build" is one editable loadout object (`PlayerLoadout`) with three parts: 4 skill slots, each a (Source × Form × Vow) triple cycled with on-screen arrows; up to 3 keystone sockets filled from whatever the Memory Dust tree has taught; and a 42-node mastery tree that is fully completable and freely respeccable. The fight is 100% automatic — nothing in this system is exercised during combat, only configured before it, and the player never sees a build number that reflects any of it. Of the three weaving axes only Form actually changes how combat resolves (six genuinely different verbs in `FormBehaviour`/`SoloBattle`); Source is a single 1.5/1.0/0.667 lookup against the region's element, and Vow is a per-skill damage multiplier with a price. The mastery tree's only real content is 6 trigger-granting notables — the other 36 nodes are flat percentages — and because earned points exceed node count by mid-game, every finished character ends with all 6 notables and an identical stat block, differing only by which of 6 affinity corners they took (and that is a free, instant toggle).
playerActions: Cycle each of 4 skill slots through 6 Sources, 6 Forms, and (known Vows + none) — three separate < > widgets per card (BuildScreen.cs:162-164, PlayerLoadout.cs:56-82). Nothing forbids duplicates: 4× the same Source/Form/Vow is a legal build (Build.cs:194-200).
Remove/add skill slots (BuildScreen.cs:165-167). Slots below 4 are simply less build — no compensating benefit.

Toggle up to 3 keystones on/off, free and reversible (PlayerLoadout.cs:89-98). But only the first 3 LEARNED keystones are ever drawn or hit-tested (BuildScreen.cs:171, 421) out of 13 the Dust tree can teach.

Click mastery nodes adjacent to something already taken; at most one Mastery corner may be held at a time (MasteryTree.cs:203-211). Respec is free, instant, and unlimited (MasteryTree.cs:226-230), so the 'one Form identity' is a toggle, not a commitment.

Buy Memory Dust nodes elsewhere (Prestige screen). This is the only permanent, unrefundable decision in the whole build system (MemoryDust.cs:126-133) and it is what unlocks Vows and keystones existing at all.
Pick which region to farm (Map screen) — that sets the enemy Source the Source axis is matched against (Game1.cs:1202) and the attack bias/tempo (SoloExpedition.cs:60-65).
During combat: nothing. The build screen is the entire input surface.
numbers: Form base damage — Strike 45, Projectile 38, Aura 22, Trap 55, Mark 0, Transformation 30 (ResonanceWeaving.cs:115-123)
Form cooldowns ms — Strike 2000, Projectile 900, Aura 0/passive, Trap 3000, Mark 4000, Transformation 2500 (FormBehaviour.cs:45-53)

Derived base DPS from those two tables: Projectile 42.2/s, Strike 22.5/s, Aura 22/s (11 per 500ms tick, FormBehaviour.cs:59 + SoloBattle.cs:276-279), Trap 18.3/s at a 1500ms bite cadence, Transformation 12/s, Mark 0. Projectile is ~1.9× Strike before any modifier.
Affinity multiplier by cyclic Form distance — 2.00 / 1.15 / 0.75 / 0.45 (FormBehaviour.cs:110-116). Applied to skills only; auto-attacks pass no Form (SoloBattle.cs:199-201).
Source matchup — 1.5× strong (delta 1-2), 0.667× weak (delta 4-5), 1.0× self/opposite (ResonanceWeaving.cs:112-113, 148-161). Six regions, one per Source (Regions.cs:38-68).
Conditional Vow multiplier = 1 + 1.5 × (1 − uptime)^1.0 (ResonanceWeaving.cs:102-103, 171-177)

Vow catalog (ResonanceWeaving.cs:249-303): BLOODIED uptime 0.25 → 2.125× below 40% HP; BOUND uptime 0.25 → 2.125× vs bosses; UNBROKEN uptime 0.60 → 1.6× above 70% HP; PATIENCE uptime 0.60 → 1.6× after 10,000ms elapsed

Static Vow multiplier = 1 + 3.0 × eHP-fraction (ResonanceWeaving.cs:107, 189-190). FRAGILITY 0.111 → 1.333× damage, +12.5% damage taken per skill carrying it, multiplied (SoloBattle.cs:169-171). RECKLESS OFFERING 0.15 → 1.45× damage, ×0.85 max HP per skill carrying it, multiplied, floored at 0.05 (SoloBattle.cs:402-410).
Resonance affinity scaling: base power × (1 + 0.008 × resonance) (ResonanceWeaving.cs:110, 202-203). Base stat 10, +2/rank (HunterProgression.cs:30, 44) → 1.08× at rank 0, +1.6% per rank.

13 keystones, 3 sockets (Keystones.cs:29-124; Build.cs:223). Notable mods: GLASS CANNON 2.0 dmg / 0.5 hp; IRONCLAD 2.0 hp / 0.5 rate; TITAN 3.0 hp / 0.4 rate; BLOOD MAGIC 2.0 rate + NoHealing; ECHO 0.6 dmg + Echo; GREED 2.0 haul / 0.7 dmg; FORTUNE 2.0 rarity / 0.75 dmg; JUGGERNAUT no mods at all, Zeal + NoHealing.
BLOODLUST scaling: ×(1 + 0.8 × missing-health-fraction); ZEAL: ×(1 + 0.8 × present-health-fraction) (SoloBattle.cs:207-221)
MARK: 1.6× amplify, 2500ms window vs 4000ms cooldown (FormBehaviour.cs:68, 76). LINGER stretches it to 4500ms (SoloBattle.cs:293) — longer than the cooldown.
TRANSFORMATION leech 0.5 of damage dealt; SIPHON ×2.0 (FormBehaviour.cs:79, SoloBattle.cs:107, 324-325)

Mastery tree: 43 nodes = 1 START + 6 arms × 6 nodes + 6 bridges; 42 spendable (MasteryTree.cs:68-121). Composition: 30 flat-stat minors, 6 notables (a trigger and BuildMods.None — MasteryTree.cs:153), 6 Mastery corners (flat stat + affinity, one at a time).

Mastery arm minor values (MasteryTree.cs:80-119): +6% to +12% damage/health/rate/spoils per node; corners +12% to +18%. Fully-walked tree products: ×2.586 damage, ×2.544 health, ×1.524 skill rate, ×1.417 haul (computed from those literals).
Mastery points earned = 3 + deepestEver/5 + conquests×5 + warrenMasteryPool (Game1.cs:1274). 6 regions × 5 = 30, so a mid-game character comfortably exceeds the 42-node tree.

Memory Dust tree: 44 nodes, 1,775 dust total (MemoryDust.cs:215-361 — the class doc at :178 still says '36 nodes totalling 1,430'). 13 keystone gates at 60 dust each, 5 vow studies (15/30/45/55/60), 15 flat stat nodes at 15/30/45.
Dust flat-stat products if fully bought: ×1.360 damage (1.08^4), ×1.331 health, ×1.260 rate, ×1.331 haul, ×1.166 rarity (MemoryDust.cs:228-349)
Crit folded to a deterministic expected value: critFactor = 1 + chance × (1.5 + 0.01×Focus − 1), chance capped at 0.75 (SoloBattle.cs:86-89, 156-159). Skill hits only.
Defense mitigation: 100/(100 + defense), applied per incoming bite (SoloBattle.cs:91, 161). Base defense is ZERO (HunterProgression.cs:46).

mods.Health is a damage-taken DIVISOR, not a pool multiplier: taken = enemyDamage / mods.Health × defenseFactor × fragilityMult (SoloBattle.cs:344). Champion.MaxHealth = hunter.MaxHealth × VowHealthMultiplier only (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:276).
Auto-attack: 6 damage every 1200ms, unaffected by Form/affinity (SoloBattle.cs:52-53, 337)
VENOM: 0.50 of each skill hit becomes poison, 0.5 of standing poison bleeds per 500ms (SoloBattle.cs:76, 78, 252-257)
EXECUTE: ×1.6 on a Strike when enemy is below 30% HP; COILED: trap cooldown ×0.5 (SoloBattle.cs:98, 100, 104)
Wave scaling: enemy 1.06^wave compounding, haul 1 + 0.35×wave linear, boss every 5th wave at ×2.2 health (WaveModel.cs:17, 20, 23, 25). Tick 100ms, ceiling 120,000ms (WaveModel.cs:29-30).
Base enemy stats at the screen: 120 health, 9 damage, 1500ms bite (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:139, SoloExpedition.cs:45)
systems.unlocks: Gated IN by the Memory Dust tree: the entire Vow axis is invisible until `vow_study_1` (15 dust, MemoryDust.cs:298) — before that `CycleVow`'s option list is literally `[null]` (PlayerLoadout.cs:74-76) and a Vow cannot be chosen; keystones each need a 60-dust gate behind 2-3 attribute nodes (MemoryDust.cs:233-355); dust itself comes only from region conquest (40 × corruption, Game1.cs:1280) and mastery-level milestones (15 each, Game1.cs:1085). Mastery points come from progress only: `3 + deepestEver/5 + conquests×5 + warrenMasteryPool` (Game1.cs:1274), so the tree is gated on depth reached and regions conquered. Gates OUT: the build is the sole determinant of how deep a run goes (`SoloExpedition.PushWave`), depth gates gleam (8 × waveScale × haul), boss cores, and boss-chest loot tier (Game1.cs:1296-1307), and depth+conquest feed back into mastery points and dust. The loop closes entirely through "how deep can this build hold".
systems.depth: Two real decisions (which Form you spam, and whether a keystone's downside is worth it) buried under ~70 free-take percentage nodes — and a strictly-correct opening exists and costs 3 points: morph_1 → morph_2 → morph_n grants ECHO (every skill fires twice, zero cost) on turn one.
gaps: BuildMods.Rarity is completely inert. It terminates in `Haul.Quality` (SoloExpedition.cs:191) and no consumer ever reads that field — Game1.cs:1235-1252 takes only Gleam and Cores. So FORTUNE (Rarity 2.0 / Damage 0.75, Keystones.cs:113), DISCERNING EYE (Rarity 2.0 / Haul 0.5, Keystones.cs:74), the fortune_1/fortune_2 dust nodes (+8% each, MemoryDust.cs:346-349), and SPLINTER's AddQuality(0.15) (SoloBattle.cs:189) are pure downside. REAPER pays SkillRate 0.75 for a trigger whose only effect is that dead quality bump (Keystones.cs:80-81).

Only 3 keystone chips are ever drawn or hit-tested (BuildScreen.cs:171 and 421, both `i < learned.Count && i < 3`), with no scrolling. 13 keystones are learnable. Once a 4th is learned it is permanently unreachable — which deletes the exact refusal DustEffects.cs:52-55 calls the point of the system ('the menu is deliberately longer than the plate').

VOW OF PATIENCE is a free +60% damage. Its `AfterElapsedMs` threshold is checked against the expedition-ABSOLUTE clock (SoloBattle.cs:419 passes `absMs`; Champion.ElapsedMs accumulates across waves at SoloBattle.cs:179), so after the first 10 seconds of a run it is permanently true — yet it is priced at 0.6 uptime for 1.6×, with no cost of any kind, on all four slots simultaneously. It is also the FIRST vow taught (15 dust). This is precisely the never-false failure the file's own comments say was already fixed twice (ResonanceWeaving.cs:50-57 and 232-247).

Mastery notables grant triggers FREE (MasteryTree.cs:153 passes BuildMods.None) that keystones charge for. morph_n grants Echo — 2× casts, no penalty — where the ECHO keystone charges Damage 0.6 (Keystones.cs:61); strike_n grants Bloodlust free where the BLOODLUST keystone charges Health 0.75 (Keystones.cs:54). Triggers are a HashSet (Build.cs:307), so socketing the keystone after taking the notable is a pure, silent penalty with zero benefit.

Nothing prevents taking ALL SIX notables. `CanTake` only blocks a second Mastery corner (MasteryTree.cs:209); the notables cost 3 points each and points exceed nodes by mid-game. Every finished character therefore carries Bloodlust + Overdraw + Radiance + Desperation + Linger + Echo simultaneously, and the 'which arm are you' question the tree's own doc comment poses (MasteryTree.cs:49-56) never gets asked.

LINGER makes MARK a permanent flat 1.6× damage stat: window 2500×9/5 = 4500ms (SoloBattle.cs:293) exceeds Mark's 4000ms cooldown (FormBehaviour.cs:51). This directly contradicts the rule written 20 lines above it ('an amplifier that is always up is not an amplifier, it is a damage stat', FormBehaviour.cs:71-76). Even without LINGER, Mark goes permanent once mods.SkillRate ≥ 1.6 — a full mastery tree (1.52) × full dust tree (1.26) = 1.92 gets there on its own.

AURA ignores SkillRate entirely — the passive branch never touches ReadyAt or mods.SkillRate (SoloBattle.cs:269-283). IRONCLAD (0.5 rate), TITAN (0.4 rate) and REAPER (0.75 rate) are therefore cost-free on an Aura build, and BLOOD MAGIC's 2× rate is worth nothing to one. Three of the tree's four 'trades' stop being trades.

MARK MASTERY is a strict downgrade. Affinity gives 2.0× to your own Form (FormBehaviour.cs:112) but Mark's base damage is 0 (ResonanceWeaving.cs:121), so the corner's headline effect multiplies nothing — while every damaging Form in the loadout eats 0.75× or 0.45×. Net: +12% damage (MasteryTree.cs:104) against a 25-55% penalty on all four skills.

Health multipliers never move the visible HP bar and never change the pool. mods.Health divides incoming damage (SoloBattle.cs:344) while Champion.MaxHealth is minted from hunter.MaxHealth × VowHealthMultiplier only (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:276). So GLASS CANNON's 'HALF HEALTH' and TITAN's 'TRIPLE HEALTH' are invisible, and they interact wrongly with BLOODLUST/ZEAL (which read health FRACTION, SoloBattle.cs:209/219) and with Transformation's flat-point leech.

'BUILD POWER' on the Build screen is `hunter.PowerRating` (BuildScreen.cs:61, 225; set at Game1.cs:1041), which is `damageMult × attackPower × 2 + defense × 2 + maxHealth × 0.5` (Gear.cs:113) — gear and trained stats only. Skills, Vows, keystones and the entire mastery tree move it by exactly zero. The one number on the build screen is blind to the build. Meanwhile `DamageBench.Measure` (Builds/DamageBench.cs) does exactly the right job by running the real sim, and has zero call sites outside tests.

The 'CORE COMPOSITION' and 'SYNERGY' panels show no numbers at all — SOURCE/FORMS/VOWS as text and a templated sentence (BuildScreen.cs:249-260). Nothing in the UI tells the player that Projectile does 1.9× Strike, that a matched Source is 1.5×, or what a Vow's multiplier is. Vow rows show only the restriction ('BELOW 40% HP'), never the power (BuildScreen.cs:284, 414).

EXECUTE, COILED, SIPHON and HARVEST are implemented in the sim (SoloBattle.cs:97-107, 149-151) but no keystone and no mastery node grants them — they come only from item enchantments (Build.cs:315-329). They are in the BuildTrigger vocabulary but unreachable from this system.
`WeaveContext.Slot` (ResonanceWeaving.cs:333) is dead — always passed 0 (SoloBattle.cs:419) and read by nothing. Left over from the deleted squad model.

Trap's cooldown gate defaults to 0 while every other skill defaults to its own cooldown (SoloBattle.cs:359 vs :286), so Trap fires on the very first bite of every wave while other Forms wait a full cycle.

The GDD (design/gdd/resonance-weaving-system.md) describes a different system entirely: 10 vows bound irreversibly at the Forge onto `charm`-type ability-focus items, a resonance resource economy, a live per-frame condition HUD, and a 6-stat Source-scaling catalog. The code has 6 vows selected by clicking an arrow, no forge binding, no resonance resource, and one scaling coefficient. design/gdd/vow-condition-tracking.md describes a tracker that does not exist.

systems.title: Memory Dust prestige tree — what it resets, what it grants, how it is earned
systems.summary: Memory Dust is not a prestige system in play — it resets nothing, has no "prestige" button, no confirmation, no run boundary, and no respec. It is a second passive-skill-tree currency that trickles in passively (overwhelmingly from Warren facilities, not from the "region mastery" faucet the code comments claim) and is spent, permanently, on a flat 44-node shopping grid worth 1,775 Dust total. Of those 44 nodes, 15 are small flat multipliers (the whole tree bought = +36% dmg / +33% HP / +26% skill rate / +33% haul), 13 are gates that teach a keystone, 5 teach Vows, and the remaining 11 are rate tweaks, two loot filters, and three nodes with no gameplay consumer at all. The only nodes that change how combat resolves are the 13 keystone gates and the 5 Vow gates — and the player can only ever wear 3 keystones, which is the one real decision the system contains. The screen presents this as a scrollable card grid sorted by category then cost, never as a graph, so the branch-vs-branch tension the catalog was authored around is invisible to the player.
playerActions: Open DUST (P key, or the hex nav) — the screen shows a Dust balance, a 3x4 scrolling card grid of all 44 nodes, and a detail panel.
Filter the grid by one of 3 categories (AMPLIFIER / EXPANSION / CONVENIENCE) or ALL (PrestigeScreen.cs:187-204). The 'RESET' button (PrestigeScreen.cs:206) resets the FILTER, not the tree.
Select a card (click or arrow keys) and press UPGRADE / Enter to buy it if affordable and its prereqs are owned (PrestigeScreen.cs:119-125, 322).
That is the entire prestige screen. No respec, no refund, no reset, no confirmation dialog, no order the player must follow beyond prereqs.

The actual build decision happens elsewhere, on the BUILD screen (B): socket up to 3 of the keystones the tree taught (BuildScreen.cs:169-177) and pick a Vow per skill from the ones the tree taught (BuildScreen.cs:158-165).
Spend Dust as a third currency on Warren facility upgrades (Game1.cs:566-572) — a sink the prestige screen never mentions.
numbers: 44 nodes, 1,775 Dust total tree cost — computed from src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Prestige/MemoryDust.cs:215-361; pinned by tests/unit/ResonanceHunter.Core.Tests/Prestige/MemoryDustTests.cs:24. The class doc at MemoryDust.cs:178 still says '36 nodes totalling 1,430' and PrestigeScreen.cs:17 still says 'the 36 unlocks' — both stale.

Node breakdown: 15 nodes carry BuildMods, 13 carry GrantsKeystone, 5 teach Vows, 4 are SHARPENED RECALL, 3 are Forge, 2 are loot filters, 2 are pure gates/no-ops (MemoryDust.cs:215-361). By UnlockEffect: 20 Amplifier, 18 Expansion, 6 Convenience.
Every stat node is one of exactly five values: Damage x1.08, Health x1.10, SkillRate x1.08, Haul x1.10, Rarity x1.08 (MemoryDust.cs:229, 239, 257, 270, 347). No node deviates.

Whole tree bought = Damage x1.08^4 = 1.360 (might_1/2/3 + blood_1), Health x1.10^3 = 1.331, SkillRate x1.08^3 = 1.260, Haul x1.10^3 = 1.331, Rarity x1.08^2 = 1.166. Combined multiplicatively via BuildMods.Combine (Build.cs:39-40) through DustEffects.TreeMods (DustEffects.cs:43-47).

One keystone dwarfs the entire stat tree: GLASS CANNON is Damage 2.0 / Health 0.5 (Keystones.cs:35); TITAN is Health 3.0 / SkillRate 0.4 (Keystones.cs:122). 13 keystones exist (Keystones.cs:29-124); Build.KeystoneSlots = 3 (Build.cs:223).
Keystone gate costs are uniform: all 13 cost 60 Dust (MemoryDust.cs:233,243,246,251,261,264,274,277,286,289,292,350,354) = 780 of the 1,775 total.
Stat-node costs by rung: rung 1 = 15, rung 2 = 30, rung 3 = 45 (MemoryDust.cs:228,230,336 and siblings). blood_1 = 20 (MemoryDust.cs:283).

Vow line: 15 / 30 / 45 / 55 / 60 = 205 Dust (MemoryDust.cs:298-307), teaching all 6 Vows in Weaving.Catalog (DustEffects.cs:103-110 vs ResonanceWeaving.cs:249-303). Vow power multipliers are the biggest numbers the tree gates: 2.125x for vow_bloodied and vow_boss_bound (uptime 0.25), 1.60x for vow_vanguard and vow_patience (uptime 0.6), 1.333x for vow_fragility, 1.45x for vow_reckless_offering — from ConditionalMultiplier = 1 + 1.5*(1-uptime) and StaticMultiplier = 1 + 3.0*cost (ResonanceWeaving.cs:171-190, tuning at 103-107).
SHARPENED RECALL: +5% region mastery rate per node, 4 nodes to +20%, costing 10/25/40/55 = 130 Dust (MemoryDust.cs:218, 310-315; DustEffects.cs:69-76).
EFFICIENT FORGE: dismantle return x1.15, hard-capped at 0.95 so it is always a loss (DustEffects.cs:86-91), applied at Game1.cs:1212-1215.
Loot filters: SORTER'S EYE (25) auto-sells Common, SORTER'S DISCIPLINE (45) auto-sells Uncommon, capped there by design (DustEffects.cs:137-143), applied at Game1.cs:1218.

EARN — Warren facilities, the dominant faucet: FORAGING PITS 450 Dust/min and SENTRY BURROWS 108 Dust/min at level 1 (Warren.cs:32, 37), times Multiplier(Dust) = 1 + 0 + conquestBonus + level*0.009 (Warren.cs:186-197). That is ~563 Dust/min at boot, credited every second via Game1.cs:541-543. The entire 1,775-Dust tree is affordable after ~3.2 minutes of idling.

EARN — region mastery ratchet: (delta total mastery levels) x 15 x (1 + corruptionTier) (Game1.cs:1080-1086). Ceiling: 6 regions (Regions.cs:38-68) x MasteryLevel 2 = 12 levels = 180 Dust lifetime at tier 0, because MasteryLevel 3 (OptimizedTeam) requires CompositionCompleteness >= 1 (RegionAutomation.cs:169) which needs a staffed 4-role team that no longer has a UI.
EARN — conquest: 40 x (1 + corruptionTier) per region conquered, at 7 waves deep (Game1.cs:1278-1280, ConquerWaveDepth = 7 at Game1.cs:1319). 240 Dust for the whole world at tier 0.
EARN — deepen corruption: 60 x max(1, tier) one-off (CorruptionScaling.cs:32-33, called Game1.cs:1748).
EARN — offline: the Warren produces at full rate while away, capped at 24 hours (SaveGame.cs:471, credited Game1.cs:391-393). An 8-hour sleep yields ~270,000 Dust — 152x the entire tree.
SPEND — the second, undocumented sink: Warren facility upgrades cost 22 x 1.25^level Dust each (Warren.cs:68-69, formula Warren.cs:132-135), spent via _dust.Spend at Game1.cs:571.

Purchase rule: affordable AND all Requires owned (MemoryDust.cs:111-117). Permanent, no refund, no respec (MemoryDust.cs:126-133). Contrast MasteryTree.Respec() which is free and instant (MasteryTree.cs:224-228).

RMP thresholds gating the mastery faucet: 500 / 2000 / 5000 (RegionAutomation.cs:13-15). The only live RMP source is RecordActiveKill at +5 flat per cleared wave (RegionAutomation.cs:11, 186; called Game1.cs:1241) — so 400 cleared waves in one region buys 2 mastery levels = 30 Dust.
systems.unlocks: Nothing gates the Dust screen — it is available from boot (Game1.cs:1014, P key) and Dust starts accruing immediately from Warren facilities that all begin at level 1 (Warren.cs:163-164). Downstream, the tree is the sole gate on two things the player would otherwise never see: the 13 keystones (DustEffects.LearnedKeystones -> PlayerLoadout.ToBuild, PlayerLoadout.cs:125-128) and all 6 Vows (DustEffects.KnownVows -> BuildScreen.cs:158, PlayerLoadout.CycleVow). It also gates the two loot filters and the Forge auto-merge. It gates zero content, zero regions, zero combat systems.
systems.depth: Two real choices exist and neither lives on this screen: which 3 of 13 keystones to wear, and which Vow to hang on each skill — the other 31 nodes are a flat, strictly-correct shopping list you finish in ~3 minutes of idle time.
gaps: BuildMods.Rarity is computed and thrown away. SoloExpedition.cs:191 folds it into Haul.Quality, Game1.cs:1236-1240 reads only Haul.Gleam and Haul.Cores, and DropBossChest (Game1.cs:1296-1308) rolls loot tier from region ladder / progression / depth / corruption while ignoring Haul.Quality entirely; Chest.cs:184 derives quality from the chest's own rarity instead. Consequence: fortune_1 + fortune_2 (45 Dust) do nothing, and two 60-Dust keystones are pure downside — FORTUNE is -25% damage for nothing (Keystones.cs:113) and DISCERNING EYE is -50% haul for nothing (Keystones.cs:74).

All 4 SHARPENED RECALL nodes (130 Dust) are dead on a fresh save. MasteryRate only enters RegionAutomation.Tick (RegionAutomation.cs:230), and Game1.cs:529 and 419 both skip any region with Team.Count == 0. The creature-assignment UI is retired (Game1.cs:147-148 comment; Game1.cs:1516 routes the A key to the Warren dashboard instead), so no farm is ever staffed. The one surviving RMP source, RecordActiveKill (RegionAutomation.cs:186), is a flat +5 that masteryRate never touches.

Three nodes have zero game-code consumers. DustEffects.ShowExactNumbers (ledger, 20 Dust), ShowMergePreview (forge_insight, 25 Dust) and TreeComplete (attunement, 45 Dust) are called only from tests (DustEffectsTests.cs:267-285). Their descriptions were already reworded to 'GROUNDWORK' / 'OPENS THE...' to stop lying, but attunement's 'A QUIET MARK THAT YOU HAVE SEEN ALL OF IT' (MemoryDust.cs:360) marks nothing — nor is MemoryDustTree.IsComplete (MemoryDust.cs:147) read anywhere in src, despite the doc comment promising 'a player deserves to KNOW when they are finished'.

The tree's own wiring test cannot catch the above. DustEffects.WiredIds (DustEffects.cs:194-200) auto-passes every node that merely carries a Mods or GrantsKeystone field, and the rest come from a hand-maintained NamedWires set (DustEffects.cs:185-192). A node is 'wired' if DustEffects reads it — not if anything downstream of DustEffects does.

The keystone refusal is designed but not presented. Build.KeystoneSlots = 3 of 13 learnable, and Build.cs:204-222 argues at length that this is the point — but BuildScreen.cs:171 and 420 both loop 'i < learned.Count && i < 3', so only the first three keystones in catalog order are ever drawn or clickable. Buy the fourth keystone gate and you cannot reach it.

The Warren silently replaced the designed faucet. MemoryDust.cs:95-97 states 'This is the ONLY faucet: Dust comes from mastering regions', and MemoryDustTests.cs:58 asserts a test named test_the_only_way_to_gain_dust_is_mastery. In the shipped game, mastery + conquest + corruption together yield a few hundred Dust over the whole campaign while FORAGING PITS alone pays 450/min from the first second — roughly 99.9% of income arrives through AwardFromMastery calls that have nothing to do with mastery (Game1.cs:393, 543).

The tree collides with a second, cheaper passive tree. MasteryTree (MasteryTree.cs) hands out the same BuildMods on the same five axes, is free to respec (MasteryTree.cs:224-228), and its notables grant BuildTrigger.Echo, Bloodlust, Overdraw, Radiance, Desperation and Linger with NO downside (MasteryTree.cs:88-110, notable Mods hardcoded to BuildMods.None at MasteryTree.cs:154). The Dust keystones ECHO (60 Dust, x0.6 damage, Keystones.cs:61) and BLOODLUST (60 Dust, x0.75 health, Keystones.cs:54) sell the identical trigger with a permanent tax attached.

auto_merge's description says 'AUTO-MERGE RUNS AFTER EVERY EXPEDITION' (MemoryDust.cs:326) but it is wired to _forge.AutoMergeOnOpen (Game1.cs:1219) — it fires when a chest is opened, not after an expedition.

The design doc bears no resemblance to the code: design/gdd/memory-dust-prestige-system.md:24 specifies 19 unlocks at 660 Dust across six named categories with milestone values {3,7,20,50} and roster-slot unlocks. The code ships 44 nodes at 1,775 Dust across three categories with a 15-per-mastery-level award and no roster.

systems.title: Items: slots, rarity, traits, affixes, enchants, upgrade and merge
systems.summary: In play, "items" is: watch the auto-battler, wait for a boss wave (every 5th) to maybe drop a chest (30–60%), press OPEN, get 1–2 pieces, then decide equip / sell / dismantle / merge / refine / reforge in the Forge. An item is 5 rolled facts — rarity, item level, element, one trait, one enchant (Rare+) — plus 0–4 affixes, and all of trait/enchant/affixes are pure FNV-1a hashes of the InstanceId, so a drop is completely frozen at mint and the only way to change it is to pay materials to re-roll (Reforge) or destroy it (Merge, which re-hashes everything because it mints a new id). Rarity is the dominant axis by a wide margin: it multiplies the weapon damage bonus (0.20 → 7.00, a 35× spread), sets affix COUNT, gates enchants entirely, and scales every trait's upside. The only genuinely build-shaping content is the 6 Form-combo enchants (Overdraw/Linger/Radiance/Execute/Coiled/Siphon), each of which is literally inert unless you wove that Form — and they live in exactly two of the eight slots' pools with no way to target them except paying 45–260 material to re-roll blind. Meanwhile the game's own "is this an upgrade?" signal (PowerRating) is blind to traits, skill rate, haul, crit, damage-%, and every enchant, so the EQUIP BEST button and the green ▲ badge rank 6 of the 8 slots purely on whether they happened to roll a Defense affix.
playerActions: Press OPEN / OPEN ALL on accumulated boss chests (ForgeScreen.cs:1071-1072). This is the only item faucet in live play — Game1.cs:1254 DropBossChest is the sole caller path.
Click a loot card, then click one of EQUIP / SELL / DISMANTLE / MERGE(3→1) (ForgeScreen.cs:1180-1197). Keyboard equivalents S / D / Space / M (ForgeScreen.cs:325-328).

Choose disposal per item: SELL for Gleam (full SellValue) vs DISMANTLE for material at 0.4× (Forge.cs:31). This is a real fork only because the two currencies buy different things; there is no numeric trade-off to reason about, the ratio is fixed.

Queue three same-rarity items into the merge tray and press MERGE, or press AUTO-MERGE ALL to do it exhaustively (ForgeScreen.cs:1245, 1255). The merge PREVIEW tells you the output type and element (ForgeScreen.cs:1235-1238) but NOT the affixes/trait/enchant, which are re-rolled.
Press J to SALVAGE JUNK — mass-dismantles every non-worn Common/Uncommon (ForgeScreen.cs:418-438).
UPGRADE mode: press UPGRADE +1 iL (Scrap + Gleam) or hold Shift for GREATER UPGRADE +5 iL (1 Crystal + Gleam) (ForgeScreen.cs:843-846).

REFORGE mode: RE-ROLL the trait (Essence) or RE-ROLL the enchant (Core, or Crystal on a Legendary) (ForgeScreen.cs:921-938). The roll always excludes the current value (Reforge.cs:126-132) but is otherwise blind.
On the Gear screen: click an inventory cell to select, click EQUIP; click a worn slot twice to unequip; or press EQUIP BEST / UNEQUIP ALL (CharacterScreen.cs:157-164).
Cycle the loot filter (TAB / filter button): ALL / WEAPONS / ARMOUR / TRINKETS / MATERIALS / RARE+ (ForgeScreen.cs:126-143). Pure view-narrowing, no mechanical effect.
numbers: 8 wearable slots: Weapon, Charm, Focus, Helm, Chest, Gloves, Boots, Ring — src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Economy/Gear.cs:17
RarityPower curve 0.20 / 0.50 / 1.20 / 3.00 / 7.00 (Common→Legendary) — Gear.cs:69-77. This single number drives weapon damage, charm def/hp, trait upside, enchant magnitude, and chest quality tilt.
WeaponDamageMultiplier = 1 + RarityPower × ItemLevelFactor → a Legendary weapon at iL1 is ×8.0 damage; a Common is ×1.2 — Gear.cs:95. Rarity of ONE item is a 6.7× damage swing.
ItemLevelFactor = 1 + (iL−1) × 0.012, UNCAPPED — Gear.cs:91. At iL60 = 1.708; at iL400 = 5.79, making that Legendary weapon ×41.5.

CharmDefenseBonus = RarityPower × 12 × ILF → Legendary iL1 = 84 Defense — Gear.cs:99. With base Defense 0 (HunterProgression.cs:46) and mitigation K=100 (SoloBattle.cs:92), one Legendary charm alone cuts incoming damage to 100/184 = 54%.

CharmHealthBonus = RarityPower × 25 × ILF → Legendary iL1 = +175 HP on a 100 base — Gear.cs:103. The charm slot also separately multiplies toughness via CharmToughness = 1 + 0.06×RarityPower×ILF (HunterProgression.cs:250-251), so the charm triple-dips: flat HP pool, damage-taken divisor, and trait/affix Health mult.

PowerRating = dmgMult×AttackPower×2 + Defense×2 + MaxHealth×0.5 — Gear.cs:114. It reads ONLY the weapon's rarity/ilvl, Defense (charm + Defense affixes), and MaxHealth (charm). It does not read WornMods (traits), SkillRate, Haul, Crit, Damage-%, or any enchant.

Consequence of the above: Hunter.PowerContribution (HunterProgression.cs:162-172) — the number behind EQUIP BEST (CharacterScreen.cs:183-184), the green ▲ (CharacterScreen.cs:339), the 'UP' badge (ForgeScreen.cs:1117-1119) and the ITEM POWER row (CharacterScreen.cs:393) — is exactly 0 for any Helm/Chest/Gloves/Boots/Ring/Focus that did not roll a Defense affix, regardless of its trait or enchant.
Affix count by rarity: 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 — ItemAffixes.cs:36-44. Commons carry nothing at all.

Affix base magnitudes: Damage +0.04, Health +0.05, SkillRate +0.03, Haul +0.06, Crit +1.5%, Defense +8 flat — ItemAffixes.cs:47-55. Scaled by ilvlFactor = 1 + iL×0.04 (ItemAffixes.cs:58,76), rarityFactor = 0.6 + RarityPower×0.10 (ItemAffixes.cs:77, so 0.65 Uncommon → 1.30 Legendary), and variance 0.75–1.25 (ItemAffixes.cs:85).
Affix stat is drawn uniformly from 6 stats per slot with duplicates allowed — ItemAffixes.cs:75, 84. A 4-affix Legendary can and does roll four Defense affixes.
Worked affix value: Legendary Damage affix at iL1 = 0.04×1.04×1.30×[0.75..1.25] = +4% to +7% DMG. At iL60 = +13% to +22%.

10 GearTrait values but only 3 pools of 4 — GearTraits.cs:7, 47-49. PoolFor (GearTraits.cs:51-56) sends Weapon→{Keen,Heavy,Swift,Savage}, Charm→{Warding,Vital,Greedy,Wild}, and everything else (Focus, Helm, Chest, Gloves, Boots, Ring — 6 of 8 slots) to the SAME pool {Attuned,Focused,Swift,Greedy}.

Trait upside up = 1 + 0.10 × RarityPower (GearTraits.cs:117) → Common 1.02, Legendary 1.70. Downsides are FLAT constants: Heavy = (dmg up×1.15, skill 0.80); Focused = (dmg 0.85, skill up×1.20); Swift = (dmg 0.90, skill up×1.10); Greedy = (hp 0.85, haul up×1.20); Wild = (dmg up×1.10, hp 0.70, skill up×1.10); the three no-drawback traits (Keen/Vital/Attuned) get only half the upside — GearTraits.cs:122-134.
Six Legendary FOCUSED items (the 6 shared-pool slots) = skill rate ×(1.70×1.20)^6 = ×72, damage ×0.85^6 = ×0.377. Traits stack multiplicatively across all 8 slots — HunterProgression.cs:196.

But SkillRate saturates hard: TickMs = 100 (WaveModel.cs:30) and cooldowns are Strike 2000 / Projectile 900 / Trap 3000 / Mark 4000 / Transformation 2500 ms (FormBehaviour.cs:45-53), so once cd/SkillRate < 100 ms a skill fires once per tick and nothing further happens. Effective ceiling ≈ ×9 (Projectile) to ×40 (Mark). Everything above that is dead stat.

11 EnchantKinds (Enchantments.cs:25-71), gated to Rare+ (Enchantments.cs:127), drawn from 3 slot pools: Weapon {Splinter, Venom, Harvest}; Charm+Ring {Undying, Desperation, Siphon}; Focus+Helm+Chest+Gloves+Boots {Linger, Radiance, Overdraw, Execute, Coiled} — Enchantments.cs:138-154.

Enchant magnitudes: Splinter min(0.60, 0.15+0.05t), Harvest min(0.50, 0.10+0.04t), Venom min(0.75, 0.20+0.06t), Desperation min(1.00, 0.20+0.08t) where t = RarityPower; every other kind is a flat binary 1f — Enchantments.cs:183-192. So 7 of the 11 enchants do not scale with rarity at all.

Actual combat magnitudes of the Form-combo enchants: Overdraw = +1 Projectile cast (SoloBattle.cs:303); Linger = Mark window ×9/5, 2500→4500 ms (SoloBattle.cs:293, FormBehaviour.cs:68); Radiance = Aura tick ×3/5, 500→300 ms (SoloBattle.cs:274, FormBehaviour.cs:59); Execute = ×1.6 on a Strike below 30% enemy HP (SoloBattle.cs:98,101,313-315); Coiled = Trap cooldown ×0.5 (SoloBattle.cs:104,357); Siphon = Transformation leech ×2.0, 0.5→1.0 of damage (SoloBattle.cs:107,325, FormBehaviour.cs:79); Undying = survive one fatal blow at 1 HP, once per expedition, never reset (SoloBattle.cs:372-376, Champion.UndyingSpent at SoloBattle.cs:24).
Venom = max(0.50, worn magnitude) of each skill hit stored as poison, bleeding 50% per 0.5 s — SoloBattle.cs:76,79,140-143,235,252-257.
Drop table BaseRarityWeight = {700, 250, 45, 4.5, 0.5} per 1000 — LootSystem.cs:105. Tilt: weight_i ×= (1 + i×0.15×(tier−1)) × (1 + i×0.6×tilt/100) — LootSystem.cs:107-108, 303-305.

Computed Legendary ITEM roll probability: 0.05% at lootTier 1, 0.22% at tier 10, 0.33% at tier 23, ~0.37% at tier 10 with the max 40% tilt. The item roll effectively never produces a Legendary — LootSystem.cs:293-313.
Chest ItemFloorByGrade = {Common, Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic} — Chest.cs:82-83. NO chest grade floors to Legendary. Combined with the 0.3% roll, Legendary items are in practice merge-only.

Computed chest grade distribution from weights {100,40,15,4,0.5} + tier×{−6,1,2,1.2,0.5} (Chest.cs:86,89): tier 1 = 59/26/11/3.3/0.6%; tier 10 = 27/34/24/11/3.8%; tier 17+ Common hits zero; tier 23 = 0/38/36/19/7.2%.

Chest drop chance = min(0.60, 0.30 + 0.015×tier) — Chest.cs:100-102. Bosses are every 5th wave — WaveModel.cs:23. lootTier = 1 + regionIndex(0–5) + regionProgression(0–4) + wave/5 + corruptionTier + regionModifier — Game1.cs:1302-1304.

Chest contents: 1 item + 35% chance of a 2nd (Chest.cs:69,185); materials = 12 + rand(0..6) + tier/4 (Chest.cs:52-58, 176-178). Grade buys quality only: quality = 1 + RarityPower×0.14 (Chest.cs:64,184), converted to tilt ×80 capped at 40% (ExpeditionLoot.cs:19,22,67) — so grade 0 = 2.2% tilt, grade 4 = 40% (capped).

Sell values by rarity: 6 / 14 / 34 / 82 / 200 — LootSystem.cs:111. SellValue is a pure function of rarity; item level NEVER changes it (Forge.Refine returns `item with { ItemLevel + 1 }` only, Forge.cs:216-220), so an iL400 item sells and dismantles for exactly the same as an iL1 one.

Merge = exactly 3 inputs, same rarity, Legendary excluded, 3:1 — Forge.cs:104-149. The product gets a NEW InstanceId (Forge.cs:138), which re-hashes trait, enchant AND all affixes, and TraitOverride/EnchantOverride are not copied — every reforge you paid for on the inputs is destroyed. Only ItemLevel survives, as max of inputs (Forge.cs:146).

Dismantle return rate 0.4 (Forge.cs:31), sorted into a material tier by the item's rarity: Common/Uncommon→Scrap, Rare→Essence, Epic→Core, Legendary→Crystal (Material.cs:27-33, ForgeScreen.cs:533-534). So dismantling one Legendary yields floor(200×0.4) = 80 Crystal.

GREATER REFINE = +5 item levels for exactly 1 Crystal + 3×(15 + 8×lvl) Gleam — Forge.cs:224-233. One dismantled Legendary (80 Crystal) therefore buys +400 item levels, and ItemLevel has no cap anywhere in the codebase.

Ordinary REFINE = +1 iL for (4 + lvl) Scrap and (15 + 8×lvl) Gleam — Forge.cs:42,45,216-220. iL1→iL60 costs 2,006 Scrap and 15,045 Gleam; the same 59 levels via Greater Refine costs ~12 Crystal and roughly a third the Gleam. Greater Refine strictly dominates.

Reforge TRAIT costs {8, 12, 20, 45, 100} Essence by rarity — Reforge.cs:29. Reforge ENCHANT costs {0, 0, 45, 110, 260} — Reforge.cs:35 — paid in CORE for Rare/Epic and CRYSTAL for Legendary (ForgeScreen.cs:589). Core only comes from dismantling Epics (32 each), so re-rolling a RARE item's enchant costs ~1.4 destroyed Epics.

Materials trickle: +1 + wave/20 Scrap per cleared wave — Game1.cs:1250. Dust node 'efficient_forge' raises the dismantle rate ×1.15 to 0.46 (DustEffects.cs:86-91); 'filter_common'/'filter_uncommon' auto-sell at or below Common/Uncommon and are hard-capped there (DustEffects.cs:137-143); 'auto_merge' auto-merges after OPEN ALL (DustEffects.cs:148-151, ForgeScreen.cs:687).

MergeRecipe.HybridTable has 10 authored entries (MergeRecipe.cs:69-81) covering only the original 5 base types. With 10 base types there are C(10,3)=120 distinct mixtures; the other 110 fall through to HybridPriority = Weapon > Charm > Focus > Helm > Chest > Gloves > Boots > Ring > Material > Core (MergeRecipe.cs:93-98,117), i.e. 'you get back whatever the most-equippable input was'. Four of the ten authored recipes contradict that priority (e.g. Weapon+Charm+Focus → Focus, MergeRecipe.cs:74).
Merge element rule: a trio sharing one element carries it through, any mixture yields null — MergeRecipe.cs:130-136.
systems.unlocks: Nothing gates the item system itself — the Forge (F) and Gear (C) screens are always open (Game1.cs:1013-1024, no unlock check anywhere). What gates item SUPPLY is depth: chests drop only on boss waves (every 5th, WaveModel.cs:23) at 30–60% (Chest.cs:100-102), and their grade + the item roll are both driven by lootTier = 1 + regionIndex + regionProgression + wave/5 + corruptionTier + regionModifier (Game1.cs:1302-1304), so the world map and corruption ladder are the real rarity dial. What gates the Forge VERBS is material tier, and each tier has exactly one source: Essence only from dismantled Rares, Core only from Epics, Crystal only from Legendaries (Material.cs:27-33) — so enchant reforging is gated behind destroying items strictly better than the one you are improving. Downstream, items gate: the weapon damage multiplier (up to ×8 at Legendary before ilvl, Gear.cs:95), effective HP and mitigation (charm, Gear.cs:99-103 + HunterProgression.cs:250-251), skill rate (traits + affixes, HunterProgression.cs:263), crit chance (HunterProgression.cs:218 → SoloBattle.cs:157) and the 11 enchant triggers the fight asks about (Build.cs:303-329). Three Memory-Dust nodes gate quality-of-life on top: filter_common/filter_uncommon (auto-sell floor), auto_merge, efficient_forge (DustEffects.cs:86-91,137-151).
systems.depth: Two real decisions exist — "which Form-combo enchant matches my woven Forms" and "do I churn Essence on this trait" — and both are buried under an EQUIP BEST button whose ranking function cannot see either of them; everything else is rarity-sorting a bag.
gaps: SPLINTER is fully dead. SoloBattle.cs:188 calls bonus.AddQuality(0.15f) → SoloExpedition.cs:191 folds it into Haul.Quality → Game1.cs:1237-1239 credits only Haul.Gleam and Haul.Cores. Nothing anywhere reads Haul.Quality. It is 1 of the 3 enchants in the WEAPON pool, so a third of all weapon enchant rolls (and every Essence/Core spent re-rolling into it) do literally nothing. Two keystones with Rarity: 2.0 (Keystones.cs:74,113) are dead for the same reason.

Item ELEMENT never reaches combat. LootSystem.cs sets it from the region, MergeRecipe.cs:130-136 carries it through merges, and the only reads are display strings (ItemNaming.cs:97, ForgeScreen.cs:857,964, CharacterScreen.cs:380-388) plus a cosmetic 'SOURCE FOCUS 50%' row (CharacterScreen.cs:231-234). The class docs on LootSystem.cs:24-28 explicitly justify hoarding by element for merges — and the merged item's element is itself only ever displayed. The whole axis is a closed loop with no payoff.

PowerRating / PowerContribution is the game's only 'is this better' signal and is blind to traits, SkillRate, Haul, Crit and every enchant (Gear.cs:114, HunterProgression.cs:148,162-172). EQUIP BEST (CharacterScreen.cs:183-184) therefore actively mis-solves 6 of 8 slots, ranking them by Defense affix only. The doc comment at HunterProgression.cs:153-160 claims this is the correct number to compare with.

Greater Refine is an unbounded exploit: 1 Crystal for +5 item levels (Forge.cs:224-233), 80 Crystal from one dismantled Legendary (Forge.cs:31 × LootSystem.cs:111), and no ItemLevel cap anywhere. ItemLevelFactor (Gear.cs:91) and the affix ilvlFactor (ItemAffixes.cs:76) are both linear and uncapped.

Merge destroys everything the player invested in the inputs. Forge.cs:138 mints a new InstanceId, so trait, enchant and all affixes re-roll; TraitOverride/EnchantOverride are silently dropped. The merge PREVIEW (ForgeScreen.cs:1235-1238) shows only type and element, so it advertises determinism for the two axes nobody cares about while the three that matter are a blind gamble. MergeRecipe.cs:14-25 argues at length that a rolled output would make the Forge a slot machine.

Trait pool collapse: 6 of the 8 slots (Focus, Helm, Chest, Gloves, Boots, Ring) share one 4-trait pool via the `_ =>` fallthrough at GearTraits.cs:53. Five armour/jewellery slots have no identity of their own. Enchantments.cs:148-154 splits the same slots differently (Ring goes with Charm), so a Ring's trait pool and enchant pool disagree about what a Ring is.

SkillRate has an invisible hard ceiling from TickMs = 100 (WaveModel.cs:30). Past roughly ×9 (Projectile) the stat does nothing, but the UI keeps printing 'TEMPO 72.00x SKILL RATE' (StatsScreen.cs:142, SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:713) and the Forge keeps printing '+104% SKL' on the item (ForgeScreen.cs:478).

Legendary items are effectively unobtainable from drops. The roll is 0.05%–0.33% across the whole tier range (LootSystem.cs:105-108) and no chest grade floors above Epic (Chest.cs:82-83) — so the 'a Legendary is an event' curve the whole system is built around (Gear.cs:66-68) is reachable only by merging three Epics, which then re-rolls its properties.

Forge.Feed (Forge.cs:194-201) and ForgeOperation (Forge.cs:9) have no live caller — ForgeScreen.cs:1189-1190 notes FEED was retired. ForgeTuning.FeedConversionRate (Forge.cs:39) carries a 15-line justification for a verb that does not exist in the UI. Likewise IneligibleReason.VowBound is never returned (Forge.cs:92), ItemInstance.EquippedToCreatureId is never assigned non-null anywhere in src/ (only saved and restored), so the entire Universal Input Gate (Forge.cs:79-87) is a no-op. Gear.ItemScore (Gear.cs:124), MergeRecipe.HasRecipe (MergeRecipe.cs:101) and DustEffects.ShowMergePreview (DustEffects.cs:164) have no live callers.

The inventory footer reads '{n} / 64 SLOTS' (CharacterScreen.cs:359) but AddLoot (ForgeScreen.cs:288) is an unbounded AddRange — there is no bag cap, so the number is decoration and the bag grows without limit.

Enchant reforge material tiers are inverted: improving a RARE item costs 45 CORE, which only comes from dismantling EPICs (ForgeScreen.cs:576-589, Material.cs:27-33). You destroy strictly better items to fix a worse one.

The design docs describe a different system entirely. item-data-schema.md §3.3 specifies a 16-field two-table model with definition_id, status lifecycle, merged_from lineage, vow_binding_log and stackable/quantity — the code's ItemInstance (LootSystem.cs:31-92) has 9 fields and derives trait/enchant/affixes from a hash. GDD Formula 1 specifies 1–5 modifier slots (code: 0–4, ItemAffixes.cs:36-44); GDD Formula 2 specifies a hard minimum of 1 enchantment slot on EVERY rarity including Common, explicitly as an Anti-Pillar compliance value — the code gates enchants at Rare+ (Enchantments.cs:127) and gives exactly one. the-forge-system.md §3.4 marks enchantments Vertical-Slice-deferred and §3.3 marks hybrids deferred; both shipped, in different shapes than specified.

systems.title: Currencies and sinks: Gleam, Scrap/Essence/Core/Crystal, Mastery, Dust
systems.summary: Eight numeric resources exist (Gleam, Scrap, Essence, Core, Crystal, Mastery-the-tree-point, Mastery-the-Warren-pool, Memory Dust, plus dead creature Cores), but only three are on the HUD — Scrap, Dust, Gleam (Game1.cs:1671-1673). In actual play the economy is one system: the Warren facility dashboard, which mints all three headline currencies passively at rates 3-4 orders of magnitude above every other faucet and every sink, and is the only place currency is ever a real constraint. The salvage tiers are elegantly designed on paper — one material per rarity band, one verb per material (Material.cs:12-20) — but Scrap's high-volume sink is strictly dominated by Crystal's, Essence/Core/Crystal never appear outside one Forge sub-screen, and the two largest authored sinks (Gleam→stat training, 79,578 lifetime capacity; Scrap→creature Feed) have no player-reachable call site at all. Memory Dust and Mastery are nominally distinct progression currencies but are both produced by the same Warren facilities, in quantities that buy out their entire finite trees (1,775 Dust / 42 nodes) in minutes. The player's only recurring currency decision is which of eight Warren facilities to upgrade next, and even that is single-variable because Gleam is the only cost that ever binds.
playerActions: Press UPGRADE on one of 8 Warren facility cards (WarrenScreen.cs:233). This is the only recurring currency decision in the game. It costs Gleam+Mastery+Dust simultaneously (Warren.cs:132-135), but only the Gleam term (5300x1.50^L) ever binds — Mastery (43x1.25^L) and Dust (22x1.25^L) grow slower than the production they buy, so those two columns are decorative.

Press UPGRADE (+1 iL) or Shift+UPGRADE (GREATER, +5 iL) on a selected item in the Forge (ForgeScreen.cs:836-843). Not a real choice: Greater strictly dominates — 24*iL+45 gold vs 40*iL+155 gold per 5 levels, and 0 Scrap vs 5*iL+30 Scrap.

Press D to dismantle one item, or J to bulk-salvage every Common/Uncommon (ForgeScreen.cs:327,329). Choosing dismantle vs sell (S) is the one authored trade in the material economy — 0.4x into a material tier vs 1.0x into Gleam.

Reroll an item's TRAIT (Essence) or ENCHANT (Core / Crystal on a Legendary) in the Forge REFORGE mode (ForgeScreen.cs:553,577). Real, but low-frequency — each material is minted by exactly one rarity of dismantle and spent on a different rarity's item.
Click nodes in the Mastery tree (BuildScreen.cs:150) and the Dust tree (PrestigeScreen.cs:140). Both are cost-free in practice: the currencies for both are overproduced by the Warren within minutes.
Press RESET on the Mastery tree — free, instant, unlimited (MasteryTree.cs:226-230).
numbers: Warren facility base rates, per minute at level 1: Gleam 520+480+410+370=1,780; Mastery 122+118=240; Dust 450+108=558 (Warren.cs:30-37). With the level-1 Warren multiplier (Warren.cs:186-197) that is ~108,936 Gleam/hr, ~14,587 Mastery/hr, ~33,781 Dust/hr — before any facility upgrade.

Warren facility upgrade cost: Gleam 5,300 x 1.50^Level; Mastery 43 x 1.25^Level; Dust 22 x 1.25^Level (Warren.cs:64-69, 132-135). First upgrade = 7,950g / 54 mastery / 28 dust. Facility L20 = 17.6M gleam / 1,908 mastery / 976 dust — i.e. the dust cost at L20 is ~2 seconds of the same Warren's dust output.

Region-farm auto-sell cap: AutoSellGleamCapPerHour = 24 (RegionAutomation.cs:33). Six regions = 144 Gleam/hour maximum from the entire automation system — 756x less than the Warren's Gleam alone. Its own doc-comment says the cap 'defuses a genuine inflation bomb'; the Warren reintroduced it 4,500x over.

Champion Gleam per cleared wave: 8 * HaulScale(w) * haul (SoloExpedition.cs:190), HaulScale = (1+0.35w) * 2.2-if-boss (WaveModel.cs:99-100). ~64 Gleam at wave 20, ~148 at wave 50. Offline champion pays 0.5x its measured live rate (Game1.cs:399), capped at 24h (SaveGame.cs:471).

Stat training: BaseTrainingCost 25, TrainingGrowthRate 1.05, StatRankCap 60 (HunterProgression.cs:17-19). 8,842 Gleam per stat x 9 stats = 79,578 lifetime sink (TotalLifetimeSink, HunterProgression.cs:324-328) — asserted by test to be '>50,000, big enough to absorb the faucet' (LootSystemTests.cs:197). That is 44 minutes of level-1 Warren Gleam, and it is unreachable anyway (see gaps).

Dismantle return 0.40 (Forge.cs:31), so per item: Common 2 Scrap, Uncommon 5 Scrap, Rare 13 Essence, Epic 32 Core, Legendary 80 Crystal (RaritySellValue {6,14,34,82,200}, LootSystem.cs:111). With EFFICIENT FORGE (40 Dust) x1.15 -> 2/6/15/37/92 (DustEffects.cs:89).

REFINE: Scrap 4+iL, Gold 15+8*iL (Forge.cs:42,45,212-221). GREATER REFINE: 1 Crystal + 3*(15+8*iL) gold for +5 iL (Forge.cs:224-233). Five Refines cost 40*iL+155 gold and 5*iL+30 Scrap; one Greater costs 24*iL+45 gold and 0 Scrap. Greater is cheaper on every axis at every level, and one Legendary dismantle (80 Crystal) buys 400 item levels.

Reforge costs: TraitCost {8,12,20,45,100} Essence, EnchantCost {0,0,45,110,260} (Reforge.cs:29,35). Enchant tier is Crystal for Legendary, Core otherwise (ForgeScreen.cs:588). So rerolling a Rare's enchant (45 Core) requires destroying ~1.4 Epic items; a Legendary trait reroll (100 Essence) requires ~7.7 Rares.

Mastery tree: 43 nodes total (MasteryTree.cs:68-121) — 1 free START, 24 arm minors, 6 bridges, 6 Mastery corners (all flat BuildMods), 6 Notables (the only nodes granting a BuildTrigger). Only one Mastery corner may ever be taken (MasteryTree.cs:209), so the practical maximum is 37 taken nodes. 36 of the 42 spendable nodes are flat +6% to +18% Damage/Health/SkillRate/Haul; 6 change how combat resolves.

Mastery tree points are DERIVED every frame as 3 + deepestWave/5 + conqueredRegions*5 + (int)warrenMasteryPool (Game1.cs:1274). The Warren mints 243 mastery/min, so the entire 42-node tree is affordable after ~10 seconds of play. The same pool is also the Warren's own upgrade currency (Game1.cs:570), and Available clamps at 0 rather than un-taking nodes (MasteryTree.cs:178) — spend the pool on facilities after buying the tree and you keep both.

Dust tree: 44 nodes, 1,775 total Dust (MemoryDust.cs:215-361) — 13 keystone gates at 60 each (780), 15 flat-multiplier nodes (+8% dmg / +10% hp / +8% skill / +10% haul / +8% rarity), 16 convenience/unlock nodes. Its own doc says '36 nodes totalling 1,430' (MemoryDust.cs:178) — stale by 8 nodes and 345 Dust. The whole tree is 3.2 minutes of level-1 Warren Dust output.

Dust faucets outside the Warren: 15 per region-mastery-level x (1+corruptionTier) (Game1.cs:1085); 40 x mult per region conquered (Game1.cs:1280); 60 x tier per corruption deepening (CorruptionScaling.cs:32-33). RMP thresholds are 500/2000/5000 and active waves pay 5 RMP each (RegionAutomation.cs:11-15,186), so ~2,400 champion waves across 6 regions yields at most 12 mastery levels = 180 Dust. The Warren makes that in 19 seconds.

Scrap faucets: 1 + wave/20 per cleared wave (Game1.cs:1252); chests pay 12 + rand(0..6) + tier/4 (Chest.cs:52,55,58,176-178) at a 30%-rising-to-60% boss drop chance (Chest.cs:100-102). Refining one item from iL1 to iL60 costs 2,070 Scrap + 15,540 Gleam cumulative.

SellValue is fixed at mint from rarity alone (LootSystem.cs:36,221) and is never touched by Refine (Forge.cs:217) or Merge (Forge.cs:142). An iL500 Legendary still sells for 200 and dismantles for 80 Crystal — every Gleam and Scrap poured into item level is unrecoverable.
systems.unlocks: Nothing gates currency access: all 8 nav destinations — Forge, Warren, Dust tree, Build tree — are open from frame one with no unlock check (Game1.cs:1880-1893). Currency gates almost nothing back: region unlock is wave-depth 7 (Game1.cs:1277,1318), corruption deepening requires all regions conquered (Regions.cs:201), and both pay currency rather than cost it. The only real currency gates are rarity gates inside the Forge (enchant reforge is Rare+, Legendary cannot merge, Forge.cs:125) and the Dust tree's prerequisite graph, which is what actually paces keystones, Vows and loot filters. Everything else is gated by wave depth or by the Warren's own compounding cost curve.
systems.depth: Almost none — one recurring decision (which Warren facility to upgrade) with one binding cost (Gleam), inside a system that prints that Gleam faster than any sink can drain it.
gaps: GLEAM'S HEADLINE SINK IS UNREACHABLE. Hunter.Train() has zero player-facing call sites: the only calls in src/ are inside the RH_SHOT_MODE screenshot-fixture block (Game1.cs:761-775, guarded at Game1.cs:653) and the save-restore replay (SaveGame.cs:447). StatsScreen.cs:22-23 says outright 'stat TRAINING (hunter.Train) is intentionally not here — flagged for the owner, since it currently has no other home.' SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:260 says it 'moved to the CHARACTER screen (press C)'; CharacterScreen has only Loadout/Equipped/Inventory/Detail panels (CharacterScreen.cs:57-61).
