The help screen still tells the player 'SPEND GLEAM ON COMMAND TO STRENGTHEN YOUR CHAMPION' (Game1.cs:1813) and the key legend still reads 'V — STATS — TRAIN' (Game1.cs:1783). There is no COMMAND screen anywhere in the source. All 9 stats DO feed combat (SoloBattle.cs:136,157,159,161; HunterProgression.cs:233,238,263,269) — they are simply frozen at base rank forever.

SCRAP'S FEED SINK IS UNREACHABLE. Feed spends 10 Scrap into a creature's evolution (AutomationScreen.cs:257,272), but AutomationScreen is dormant — Game1.cs:147-148: 'The old creature den (_automation) is retired from the UI; _automation is kept only to carry the saved roster/cores forward.' ForgeScreen.cs:1189 confirms 'FEED was retired'. Nav slot 5 is labelled WARREN but routes to the facility dashboard (Game1.cs:1516). Scrap's only live sink is REFINE, which Greater Refine dominates.

CREATURE CORES ARE A DEAD CURRENCY. Boss waves mint 2*haul Cores (SoloExpedition.cs:186), credited to _automation.Cores (Game1.cs:1240). The only consumer is Hatch() on the dormant AutomationScreen (AutomationScreen.cs:226-227). They accumulate forever, are saved, and are never spendable. They are not shown on the HUD.

THE ENTIRE REGION-FARM FAUCET IS DEAD ON A FRESH SAVE. Region.Assign() is only reachable from the dormant AutomationScreen (AutomationScreen.cs:213-214) and from save restore (Game1.cs:371,379). SeedNewGame creates 3 starter creatures and assigns none (Game1.cs:468-478) while its comment claims 'The starter creatures staff the WARREN now (the idle farm)'. TickFarms skips any region with Team.Count == 0 (Game1.cs:530), so kills, cores, the 24g/hr auto-sell and work-tick RMP all produce zero, permanently.

SHARPENED RECALL I-IV (130 Dust) BUY NOTHING IN PRACTICE. DustEffects.MasteryRate (DustEffects.cs:69-76) is passed only into Region.Tick's masteryRate parameter (Game1.cs:420,532), which multiplies work-tick RMP — unreachable per the above. The reachable RMP path, RecordActiveKill (RegionAutomation.cs:186, called at Game1.cs:1241), does not apply masteryRate at all.

90 DUST OF NODES STILL DO NOTHING. HUNTER'S LEDGER (20), FORGE INSIGHT (25) and COMPLETE ATTUNEMENT (45) are 'wired' only in the sense that DustEffects.ShowExactNumbers / ShowMergePreview / TreeComplete exist (DustEffects.cs:157-175); grep shows zero call sites outside DustEffects.cs. The catalog's own comment (MemoryDust.cs:208-213) claims 'tests assert every id here is reachable from DustEffects' — the test checks a hand-maintained NamedWires string set (DustEffects.cs:185-192), not that anything consumes the return value. This is the exact failure mode the class was written to prevent, recurring.

OPTIMIZED TEAM MASTERY LEVEL IS UNREACHABLE. It requires CompositionCompleteness() >= 1f (RegionAutomation.cs:169), which requires a staffed 4-role team, which requires the dormant screen. Every region caps at FullyMastered, halving the mastery-level Dust faucet's ceiling (Game1.cs:1081-1087).

MASTERY IS TWO CURRENCIES SHARING ONE NAME AND ONE VARIABLE. _warrenMasteryPool is both the Warren's spendable balance (Game1.cs:566,570) and an addend into the build tree's derived point total (Game1.cs:1274). The Warren screen labels it 'MASTERY' (WarrenScreen.cs:66) and the Build screen labels the same number 'POINTS' (BuildScreen.cs:378) with no indication they are linked. Spending in the Warren silently reduces build-tree points; if the pool falls below nodes already taken, Available clamps to 0 and the nodes are kept for free.

CURRENCY NAMING IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS SCREENS. WarrenScreen calls Gleam 'GOLD' and Memory Dust 'NATURE' (WarrenScreen.cs:66, 174, 221-223); the HUD, Forge and Prestige screens call them GLEAM and MEMORY DUST. The Forge's own messages mix 'g' and 'GLEAM' (ForgeScreen.cs:602,622).

ESSENCE / CORE / CRYSTAL ARE INVISIBLE OUTSIDE ONE PANEL. The HUD carries only Scrap, Dust and Gleam by explicit decision (Game1.cs:1662-1665); the other three tiers appear only in the Forge UPGRADE mode's 4-cell strip (ForgeScreen.cs:809-818). A player never sees their Crystal count while deciding whether to salvage a Legendary.

GREATER REFINE IS HIDDEN BEHIND AN UNDOCUMENTED SHIFT MODIFIER (ForgeScreen.cs:836) and its afford-check omits the Crystal term (canGreat at ForgeScreen.cs:837 tests only Gleam) — harmless today only because doGreat separately requires hasCrystal.

PRECISION RISK: _warrenMasteryPool is a long, cast to int when fed to SetEarned (Game1.cs:1274). At high facility levels (~1.8M mastery/hr around facility L50) this overflows in roughly a thousand hours of accumulated idle time.

systems.title: Regions, conquest, corruption ladder and region mastery automation
systems.summary: Six hardcoded regions in a strict linear chain (Regions.cs:38-69). You "conquer" one by letting your auto-battling champion reach wave 7 in it (Game1.cs:1277, 1318) — there is no boss fight, no objective, no choice; the champion fights on a timer while you watch or don't. Conquest is a one-shot latch that unlocks the next region, pays 40 Memory Dust, +5 mastery-tree points, and +10% Warren production; regions differ only by three numbers (a ladder index multiplier, an attack-tempo enum, and a flat health/damage/loot-tier modifier record). Once all six are conquered a DEEPEN button appears that increments a global corruption tier — an uncapped, cost-free, no-confirmation ratchet that pays 60×tier Dust per press and multiplies enemy HP and damage by (1+0.6×tier). The entire "region mastery automation" half of this system — RMP accrual from creature work-ticks, the four-role composition puzzle, the 25/40→100/120% idle-efficiency bands, the auto-sell cap, the per-region farm teams — is fully implemented in Core and **completely unreachable in the shipping build**: `AutomationScreen` is constructed (Game1.cs:596) and never `Update()`d or `Draw()`n (the A/WARREN nav slot draws the facility dashboard instead, Game1.cs:1119-1125, 1516), so no creature can ever be assigned to a farm, so `TickFarms` skips every region forever (Game1.cs:530).
playerActions: Open MAP (W key or nav slot 6), cycle regions with Left/Right or click a row/node, press ENTER REGION to set the active region. This is the only navigational decision in the system.

Decide whether to stay in a conquered region (depth keeps climbing → better loot tier, more RMP) or travel (resets your wave to 1 — SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:247-252 nulls the run and zeroes Deepest whenever EnemySource changes).
Press D or click DEEPEN once all six regions are conquered. Repeatable immediately, unlimited, free, no confirm dialog (MapScreen.cs:104, 310; Game1.cs:1743-1751).

That is the complete action set. Everything else in this system is watched, not chosen: conquest fires automatically at wave 7, mastery accrues automatically at +5 RMP/wave, corruption/region modifiers apply automatically.
numbers: 6 regions, hardcoded, strictly linear via PrereqId — verdant_hollow → cinderworks → umbral_reach → marrow_wastes → still_archive → pale_choir (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Encounters/Regions.cs:38-69). No branching, no optional regions.

Conquest threshold: reach wave 7 in the active region (Game1.cs:1318 `ConquerWaveDepth = 7`; checked Game1.cs:1277). Boss waves are every 5th wave (WaveModel.cs:23), so conquering a region = clearing exactly one boss plus two trash waves.

Conquest rewards: 40 × RewardMultiplier Memory Dust (Game1.cs:1280), +5 mastery-tree points per region (Game1.cs:1274 `_world.ConqueredIds.Count * 5`), +10% to ALL Warren facility production per region (Warren.cs:75 `ConquestBonusPerRegion = 0.10f`, applied Warren.cs:194).

Region ladder scaling is the only real per-region difficulty: enemyBaseHealth = 110 × (1+0.35×regionProgression) × (1+0.35×ladderIndex) × corruptionScale × modHealth; enemyBaseDamage = 9 × (1+0.20×regionProgression) × (1+0.25×ladderIndex) × corruptionScale × modDamage (Game1.cs:1228-1229; ladderIndex = position in Regions.All, Game1.cs:1177-1182). Region 6 vs region 1 at equal mastery is 2.75× HP and 2.25× damage — the entire world spread.

regionProgression = clamp((int)MasteryLevel + (MasteryLevel>0 ? 1 : 0), 0, 4) (Game1.cs:1030) → values 0, 2, 3, 4. It BOTH raises enemy HP/damage and raises loot tier. Fed by the active region's RMP, which in the live build comes only from RecordActiveKill = +5 RMP per cleared wave (RegionAutomation.cs:186, called Game1.cs:1241).

Mastery thresholds: 500 / 2000 / 5000 RMP (RegionAutomation.cs:13-15). At 5 RMP per wave that is 100 / 400 / 1000 waves cleared in that one region. The 5000 tier (OptimizedTeam) additionally requires CompositionCompleteness() >= 1f (RegionAutomation.cs:169) — a four-role staffed team — which is unreachable, so the ceiling is FullyMastered (level 2, regionProgression 3).

Region modifiers, 6 flat records (RegionModifiers.cs:25-30): verdant 1.10× HP / 1.0× dmg / +0 loot; cinderworks 1.20/1.0/+1; umbral 1.0/1.20/+1; marrow 1.25/1.10/+1; still_archive 1.0/1.25/+2; pale_choir 1.20/1.20/+2. Pure multipliers — zero mechanical change.

CombatBias, 3 values (AttackBias.cs:12) mapped to enemy bite tempo (SoloExpedition.cs:60-64): Heavy = 2200ms interval × 1.4667 damage, Fast = 1000ms × 0.6667, Balanced = 1500ms × 1.0. Total DPS is identical by construction — the code comment says so explicitly. Assigned: Balanced, Heavy, Fast, Heavy, Fast, Balanced (Regions.cs:44,49,53,60,64,68).

Corruption ladder (CorruptionScaling.cs): HealthMultiplier = 1 + 0.6×tier (:19), TierBonus = tier (:22), RewardMultiplier = 1 + tier (:26), DeepeningDustAward = 60 × max(1,tier) (:33). The health multiplier is applied to BOTH enemy health and enemy damage (Game1.cs:1220 → 1228 and 1229). Unbounded — nothing caps CorruptionTier (Regions.cs:207-211).

Corruption's RewardMultiplier reaches only two call sites: mastery-level Dust (Game1.cs:1084) and conquest Dust (Game1.cs:1280). Conquest Dust can never fire again once corruption > 0 (all regions already conquered), and mastery-level Dust totals at most 6 regions × 2 levels × 15 = 180 Dust for the entire game (Game1.cs:1081-1087). So the only meaningful corruption payoff is the 60×tier one-off, and the drawback (HP+damage) is permanent.

Source matchup: ×1.5 strong / ×0.667 weak / ×1.0 neutral, by (target - attacker) mod 6 (ResonanceWeaving.cs:148-161, multipliers at :112-113). Region theme sets EnemySource (Game1.cs:1202), so region choice interacts with your woven skills' Sources — this is the single deepest region-driven decision in the game and it is never surfaced on the Map screen.

Encounter templates: 4 per region (3 standard at SelectionWeight 10/10/8, 1 boss at weight 0) — Regions.cs:122-125. NOTHING spawns them. `Regions.AllTemplates` (Regions.cs:82) has zero callers. The only consumed field is ParClearTimeSeconds (Regions.cs:160-161) and Boss.PowerTierBase for two display strings (MapScreen.cs:84, 284).

Derived par clear times (EncounterSpawner.DerivePar, EncounterSpawner.cs:36-46, tuning at EncounterTemplate.cs:54-61) — standard/farm-average per region: verdant 15/13/24 → farm par 17s; cinderworks 36/29/47 → 37s; umbral 112/94/149 → 118s; marrow 257/218/336 → 270s; still_archive 622/519/794 → 645s; pale_choir 1848/1564/2416 → 1943s. Boss pars: 591 / 1936 / 9695 / 32585 / 63827 / 106262 seconds (the last is 29.5 hours). The last region's farm is authored 114× slower than the first.

Idle efficiency bands (EfficiencyContract.cs:43-50): NewlyConquered 25-40%, Partially 50-70%, Fully 80-100%, Optimized 100-120%. TeamQuality = 0.65×CCS + 0.35×PQS (RegionAutomation.cs:20-21, 155). Auto-sell cap 24 Gleam/hour PER REGION (RegionAutomation.cs:33) against gleamPerKill = 8 (Game1.cs:532) — a maxed 6-region empire would realize 144 Gleam/hour total, versus Warren facility upgrades costing 5,300 Gleam at level 1 (Warren.cs GleamCostBase). None of this executes in the live build.

MapScreen: 6 fixed serpentine node positions (MapScreen.cs:68-71) — the map cannot render a 7th region. RECOMMENDED POWER = Boss.PowerTierBase × 350 (MapScreen.cs:84) → 1400 / 2800 / 4900 / 5950 / 6650 / 7000. `HunterPower` and `DeepestWave` are pushed to the screen every frame (Game1.cs:1725-1726) and never read anywhere in MapScreen.cs — the displayed power number is compared against nothing.

Chest drop chance = min(0.60, 0.30 + 0.015 × lootTier) (Chest.cs:100-102, 141-144), lootTier = 1 + ladderIndex + regionProgression + wave/5 + corruptionTier + modLootBonus (Game1.cs:1302-1304). Region modifiers contribute +0 to +2 of a value that saturates at 20 — i.e. the deepest region's loot-tier identity is worth at most 3 percentage points of drop chance.
systems.unlocks: Gated by: reaching wave 7 in the previous region (Game1.cs:1277), which requires nothing but a champion strong enough to survive 7 waves — no key, no cost, no boss encounter. Gates: the next region in the fixed list (Regions.cs:178-183); +5 mastery-tree points and +10% Warren production per region; and, at 6/6, the corruption ladder. Nothing else in the game is gated on region conquest — the Forge, Build, Character, Prestige and Warren screens are all open from the start.
systems.depth: Almost none: the only choices are which unlocked region to sit in (a Source-matchup and a ×1.1–1.25 stat twist) and how many times to press DEEPEN — and the automation/composition layer that was supposed to carry the depth is completely unreachable code.
gaps: **AutomationScreen is never Updated or Drawn.** It is constructed at Game1.cs:596 and its `Update()`/`Draw()` have zero callers (the A/WARREN nav slot routes to `DrawWarren()` — the facility dashboard — at Game1.cs:1119-1125 and 1516). Consequences: no creature can ever be assigned to a region farm; `TickFarms` hits `if (farm.Team.Count == 0) continue;` (Game1.cs:530) for all six regions forever; the entire RegionAutomation.Tick body, the four role stations, the RMP-per-work-tick formula, IdleEfficiencyPercent, AutomationClearTimeSeconds, the auto-sell cap and the AutomationStage 1/2/3 selector are dead in play. This is the single biggest gap in the system.

Creature cores accumulate with no sink. `_automation.Cores` is credited from every wave (Game1.cs:1240) and from offline (Game1.cs:428), is saved as `UnhatchedCores`, and the only consumer is the private `Hatch()` inside the unreachable AutomationScreen (AutomationScreen.cs:224-233). The player accrues a currency they can never spend.

`MasteryLevel.OptimizedTeam` (the 100-120% idle band, and regionProgression = 4) is arithmetically unreachable because it requires `CompositionCompleteness() >= 1f` (RegionAutomation.cs:169), which requires an assigned team, which requires the dead screen. The top rung of the mastery ladder does not exist.

The GDD's four Automation Capability Stages are supposed to be gated on mastery level (design/gdd/region-mastery-automation-system.md A5: Stage 3 requires FullyMastered, Stage 4 requires Optimized). In code `AutomationStage` is a plain settable int with a free +/- button, no cost and no gate (RegionAutomation.cs:105; AutomationScreen.cs:306-307, 329-330). "Earned, not given" is a comment, not a rule.

`region_storage_capacity` (GDD A7, default 500/resource), the Blocked/Starved work-state signals, and Stage 4 offline progression's closed-form saturation model (GDD Formula 8) are entirely absent from Core. Offline is a flat `farm.Tick(credited)` replay (Game1.cs:420) with no capacity constraint.

The GDD specifies the Stage-3 Gleam cap as GLOBAL and account-wide (A8, explicitly to prevent multiplying it by mastering more regions). The code makes it per-`Region` instance (RegionAutomation.cs:33, 301-313) — exactly the failure mode A8 was written to prevent, and the world now ships six regions.

Once all six regions are conquered, the Map's detail-panel CTA becomes DEEPEN unconditionally and the ENTER REGION button disappears (MapScreen.cs:307-313). A mouse-only player permanently loses the ability to travel between regions at endgame; the keyboard path (Enter, MapScreen.cs:103) still works.

DEEPEN has no cost, no cooldown, no confirmation, and pays 60×tier Dust immediately (Game1.cs:1743-1751). Clicking it 20 times in a row is worth 60×(1+…+20) = 12,600 Dust for a single click sequence; the drawback is a permanent ×13 enemy HP/damage.

The whole EncounterTemplate / CreaturePool / SelectionWeight / boss-health authoring layer is vestigial — the retired manual-combat spawner. Six regions × 4 templates = 24 authored encounters with per-creature IDs and health values that no code path can ever spawn. Only `ParClearTimeSeconds` survives, and it feeds only the dead farm.

`MapScreen.HunterPower` and `MapScreen.DeepestWave` are pushed every frame (Game1.cs:1725-1726) and read nowhere. The screen prints "RECOMMENDED POWER 4,900" with no comparison to the player's actual power and no gating on it.

Travelling to any region resets the wave counter and `Deepest` to 0 (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:247-252). There is no per-region depth persistence, so revisiting a conquered region always restarts the climb at wave 1 — which makes the "farm a conquered region deeper for loot" pitch (Game1.cs:1314-1316 comment) cost a full re-climb every time you look at the map and come back.

`marrow_wastes` (Source.Body) is mapped to boss art `spirit_matron` and `pale_choir` (Source.Spirit) to `lumen_angel` (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:115-119) — the Body region's boss is the spirit-themed one.

design/gdd/region-view-world-map-ui.md specifies a Region View diorama (§3.2), an aggregate summary readout (§3.3), a mastery transition presentation sequence (§3.4), map-scale problem surfacing (§3.5) and a displayed region yield rate (Formula 1). None of these exist — MapScreen.cs is a three-panel static readout with no yield display and no problem indicators.

systems.title: Warren facilities: what they produce, their costs and their curves
systems.summary: The Warren is a flat list of 8 always-unlocked facilities, each with exactly one number that changes: its level. Every facility is mechanically identical — level × authored base rate × an additive milestone bonus, feeding one of three currencies — and every facility shares the *same* upgrade cost curve (5300×1.50^L gleam / 43×1.25^L mastery / 22×1.25^L dust), so the only thing distinguishing them is the base rate constant. Production runs every frame on every screen (Game1.cs:538-545) and offline up to 24h, crediting real Gleam/Dust balances and a Mastery pool that is added straight into the mastery-tree point total. In play it is a two-verb screen: click a card, click UPGRADE, repeat; there is no timer, no queue, no adjacency, no capacity, no unlock, and no per-facility mechanic. Because cost grows 1.5× per level while output grows linearly, payback goes from 0.3h at L1→2 to 353h at L20→21 — the system self-terminates around facility L15-20 and the four non-Gleam facilities are finished at level 1.
playerActions: Click one of 8 facility cards to select it (src/ResonanceHunter.Game/WarrenScreen.cs:142). Zero cost, zero consequence — it only changes which detail panel is drawn.

Click UPGRADE to spend Gleam+Mastery+Dust for exactly +1 level on the selected facility (WarrenScreen.cs:229-230 -> src/ResonanceHunter.Game/Game1.cs:565-573). Instant, no timer, no queue, no confirmation, no bulk-buy: 1 click = 1 level.

That is the complete interaction set. There is no build/demolish, no placement or adjacency, no worker/creature assignment, no facility on/off toggle, no production-target switching, no collect/claim, and no unlock action.
The only indirect lever is conquering regions elsewhere, which the host pushes in as a flat +10%/region production bonus (Game1.cs:540, 558).
numbers: Facility catalog — 8 entries (currency, base/min): Nursery Gleam 520 (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Warrens/Warren.cs:30); Tunnels Gleam 480 (Warren.cs:31); ForagingPits Dust 450 (Warren.cs:32); ScavengerRuns Gleam 410 (Warren.cs:33); BreedingChamber Mastery 122 (Warren.cs:34); RitualNest Mastery 118 (Warren.cs:35); HoardVaults Gleam 370 (Warren.cs:36); SentryBurrows Dust 108 (Warren.cs:37). Split: 4 Gleam / 2 Mastery / 2 Dust.

Output = round(BaseRate × Level × MilestoneMultiplier) (Warren.cs:118). MilestoneTier = Level/5 (Warren.cs:106; MilestoneEvery=5 at Warren.cs:78); MilestoneMultiplier = 1 + 0.15×tier (Warren.cs:115, Warren.cs:81). Additive, so even L30 is only ×1.90 from milestones across the entire curve.

Upgrade cost L→L+1, IDENTICAL for all 8 facilities and keyed only off that facility's own level (Warren.cs:132-135): Gleam round(5300 × 1.50^L) (Warren.cs:64-65); Mastery round(43 × 1.25^L) (Warren.cs:66-67); Dust round(22 × 1.25^L) (Warren.cs:68-69). L1 = 7,950g/54m/28d; L10 = 305,625g/400m/205d; L18 = 7,832,827g/2,387m/1,221d; L25 = 133,831,192g/11,382m/5,823d.

Payback time for one Nursery upgrade from its own marginal output: L1→2 = 0.3h; L5→6 = 1.1h; L10→11 = 7.5h; L15→16 = 51h; L20→21 = 353h; L25→26 = 2,451h. Cost grows 1.5×/level, output grows ~(L+1)/L — ROI diverges exponentially (derived from Warren.cs:118 and Warren.cs:132-135).

Production multiplier is fully ADDITIVE, never multiplicative (Warren.cs:197): 1 + AllProductionBonus + ConquestBonus + ResourceBonus. AllProduction = (WarrenLevel−1)×0.03 (Warren.cs:183, Warren.cs:56). ResourceBonus = WarrenLevel × 0.02 Gleam / 0.013 Mastery / 0.009 Dust (Warren.cs:186-191, Warren.cs:57-59). Conquest = regions × 0.10 (Warren.cs:194, Warren.cs:75).

Warren XP = newFacilityLevel × 100 per upgrade (Warren.cs:224, Warren.cs:72); XpToNext = 1000 × (Level+2) (Warren.cs:177). Taking all 8 facilities to L20 yields 167,200 XP = Warren L16 = only a ×1.77 gleam multiplier. Warren level is a rounding error next to facility level.

Fresh Warren (all facilities L1, WL1, 0 regions) produces 1,816 Gleam/min, 243 Mastery/min, 563 Dust/min. The dev fixture (Game1.cs:922-930: L18/17/16/15/16/14/13/12, WL23) produces 86,019 Gleam/min, 9,752 Mastery/min, 22,637 Dust/min.

The Mastery facilities trivialize the mastery tree. The pool credits directly into tree points: SetEarned(3 + deepest/5 + conquered*5 + (int)_warrenMasteryPool) (Game1.cs:1274). The whole tree is 43 nodes = 42 spendable (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Builds/MasteryTree.cs:72-135: 1 start + 6 arms × 6 + 6 bridges), and only 1 of 6 Mastery capstones is takeable (MasteryTree.cs:209), so ~37 points buys everything useful. At 243/min that is ~10 SECONDS of Warren production.

The Dust facilities trivialize the prestige tree. Memory Dust catalog = 44 nodes totalling 1,775 dust (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Prestige/MemoryDust.cs:215+; individual costs 10-60). At 563 dust/min that is 3.2 MINUTES. Dust has exactly two sinks in the entire game: the prestige tree and Warren upgrade costs (Game1.cs:571 is the only _dust.Spend call).

Offline cap = 24h (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Persistence/SaveGame.cs:471 MaxOfflineSeconds = 24 * 3600, clamped at SaveGame.cs:473-474), credited at Game1.cs:391-394. Live production ticks every frame on every screen at Game1.cs:538-545.

Tick determinism: production carries as currency-seconds and divides by 60 once at the floor step (Warren.cs:155-158, Warren.cs:237-249), so 3600 one-second ticks == one 3600-second tick (pinned by tests/unit/ResonanceHunter.Core.Tests/Warrens/WarrenTests.cs:155-170).

Gleam facility ordering is near-lockstep, not a choice: with one shared cost curve, optimal greedy play separates Nursery (520) from HoardVaults (370) by only log_1.5(520/370) = 0.84 levels. The four Gleam facilities always sit within ~1 level of each other regardless of player skill.
systems.unlocks: Gated by nothing — all 8 facilities exist at level 1 the moment the game starts (Warren.cs:163-164), and the WARREN nav slot has no unlock condition (Game1.cs:658, 1119-1125). It gates nothing either: no other system reads Warren level or any facility level (the only FacilityKind references outside Warren.cs/WarrenScreen.cs are the dev fixture at Game1.cs:924-926). Inbound coupling is a single flat number — conquered region count → +10% production each (Game1.cs:540, 558). Outbound it is a pure faucet into Gleam (Hunter balance), Dust (prestige tree), and the Mastery pool (build-tree points, Game1.cs:1274).
systems.depth: Almost none — 8 facilities, 1 shared cost curve, 1 verb, and the optimal order is fixed by 8 authored constants; the only real decision (gleam vs mastery vs dust) resolves permanently within ~3 minutes because both non-gleam sinks are finite and tiny.
gaps: GDD/code drift on the headline cost curve: design/gdd/warren-facilities.md §4 states Gleam cost `18700 × 1.40^L`; the code is `5300 × 1.50^L` (Warren.cs:64-65). Different base AND different growth — every cost number in the GDD is wrong.

GDD §4 omits the milestone system entirely — it documents output as `round(BaseRate × L)` while the code is `round(BaseRate × L × (1 + 0.15 × (L/5)))` (Warren.cs:118, :115). The milestone feature is implemented and displayed but undocumented in the design doc's formula section.

Offline production silently drops the conquest bonus. The offline catch-up tick runs at Game1.cs:391, but `_warren.ConqueredRegions` is only ever assigned at Game1.cs:540 and Game1.cs:558 — both after load. `Warren.Restore` (Warren.cs:256-263) does not set it and it defaults to 0. So up to 24h of offline production is credited at ConquestBonus = 0, losing up to +80% (8 regions × 0.10) of the multiplier at Warren.cs:197.

Integer overflow makes late upgrades free. `UpgradeCost` casts to int (Warren.cs:133) but 5300×1.50^32 = 2,286,631,381 > int.MaxValue. At facility level 32 the gleam cost goes negative; `CanAfford` (Warren.cs:209-213) then passes trivially, `SpendGleam` rejects amount<=0 and takes nothing (src/ResonanceHunter.Core/Economy/HunterProgression.cs:296-297), yet Game1.cs:572 calls `Upgrade` anyway — free gleam upgrades from L32 up. Separately, Gleam is itself an int (HunterProgression.cs:73) capping the balance at 2.147B, so L31 (1,524,420,921) is the last level the player can even bank for.
Designed but unreachable: `Facility.OnMilestone` (Warren.cs:112) and `WarrenYield.Any` (Warren.cs:49) are dead — never referenced anywhere in src/ or tests/.

The CREATURES sub-view is documented but does not exist. GDD §3 and the WarrenScreen doc-comment (WarrenScreen.cs:15) both say the creature den is 'preserved as a sub-view reached via the CREATURES button'; there is no such button in WarrenScreen.cs, and Game1.cs:935 comments 'deprecated: the creature den was removed'.
No bulk-buy. One click = one level (WarrenScreen.cs:229). Getting 8 facilities to L20 is 152 clicks, and every single one triggers a full synchronous `Save()` (Game1.cs:573).

Displayed numbers don't reconcile. Grid cards show raw `BaseOutputPerMin` with no multiplier (WarrenScreen.cs:163) while the overview shows multiplied `ProductionPerMinute` (WarrenScreen.cs:124), so the 8 card numbers never sum to the overview total. The detail panel's 'NEXT' figure (WarrenScreen.cs:208) is also raw, understating the real gain by the full multiplier.

Three of eight flavor descriptions promise mechanics that do not exist: Nursery 'Increases gold production' implies a multiplier (Warren.cs:30); HoardVaults 'Store and compound the warren's gold' implies compounding (Warren.cs:36); SentryBurrows 'Guard the forage lines, protecting dust yield' implies protection (Warren.cs:37). All three are plain flat linear production identical to the rest.

Build timers are acknowledged as missing, not designed: Warren.cs:148 calls a timer layer 'a documented follow-up', and the UI advertises the absence as a feature — 'INSTANT UPGRADE · NO WAIT' (WarrenScreen.cs:227).

UI ceilings hit before the math does: the `Ab()` formatter has no B suffix (WarrenScreen.cs:69-71) so 1.02B gleam renders as '1016.3M', and milestone pips are capped at 5 (WarrenScreen.cs:152) so facilities at L25+ stop advancing visually.

No unit test covers the cost curve's actual values, the multiplier composition, or the payback economics — WarrenTests.cs only asserts directional inequalities (e.g. WarrenTests.cs:100-102 `dear.Gleam > cheap.Gleam`). Nothing pins the authored balance numbers, which is why the GDD could drift from 18700×1.40^L to 5300×1.50^L undetected.

systems.title: Idle/offline earnings and automation — what happens while away
systems.summary: In play, "idle" is three unrelated faucets and only one of them matters. The dominant one is the Warren facility economy: eight facilities that exist at level 1 from the first frame and immediately pay ~1,816 Gleam + 243 Mastery + 563 Dust per minute, on every screen and while the game is closed, with no gate, no unlock order, and no build timers. The second is the champion auto-battler, which pays per cleared wave live and at a flat 50% of its measured gleam/second offline. The third — the region/creature farm with its composition puzzle (CCS/PQS), mastery ladder, idle-efficiency bands and auto-sell cap — is fully implemented in Core and fully unit-tested, but is completely unreachable in the shipped build: the only code that assigns a creature to a region lives in AutomationScreen, which is never Update()d or Draw()n, so every farm's team is empty and every region tick returns on the first branch. The only real offline decision is when to come back, and the welcome-back toast doesn't even report the income that actually landed.
playerActions: Press A (WARREN) and click UPGRADE on one of 8 facilities. This is the ONLY recurring idle decision in the shipped game. It is instant — no build timers (WarrenScreen.cs:227 literally prints 'INSTANT UPGRADE · NO WAIT'; Warren.cs:220-225). The only sub-decision is which of 8 facilities to feed, and since 4 produce Gleam / 2 Mastery / 2 Dust and one currency (Gleam) is the binding constraint at every level, the answer is 'whichever Gleam facility is cheapest', i.e. all four in lockstep.

Set battle speed x1/x2/x4/x8 on the HUNT screen (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:66, 876). This directly multiplies the champion's real-time gleam/sec — and therefore the saved ChampionGleamRate that pays out offline. It is a free, uncosted 8x throughput lever.
Choose the active region on the MAP. Changes enemy scaling and loot tier (Game1.cs:1228-1229, 1302-1304); the per-region idle farm readout it also shows (MapScreen.cs:303) is inert.
Close the game and come back. Offline credit is elapsed wall-clock, clamped to 24h (SaveGame.cs:471-474).

NOT AVAILABLE despite being coded: assigning creatures to farm stations, hatching cores, setting automation stage 1/2/3, feeding/evolving creatures. All of it lives in AutomationScreen.cs, whose Update() and Draw() have zero call sites — Game1.cs:1119-1125 explicitly no-ops the screen and Game1.cs:1516 routes the WARREN nav slot to the facility dashboard instead.
numbers: Warren facility base rates per minute, all at level 1 from `new Warren()` (Warren.cs:30-37): Nursery 520 G, Tunnels 480 G, ForagingPits 450 D, ScavengerRuns 410 G, BreedingChamber 122 M, RitualNest 118 M, HoardVaults 370 G, SentryBurrows 108 D. Raw totals: 1,780 Gleam/min, 240 Mastery/min, 558 Dust/min.

Warren level-1 multipliers (Warren.cs:56-59, 183-197): AllProduction (Level-1)*0.03 = 0; per-currency Level*0.02 G / *0.013 M / *0.009 D; Conquest 0.10 per conquered region (Warren.cs:75). Net level-1 output = 1,816 Gleam/min, 243 Mastery/min, 563 Dust/min → 108,936 Gleam/hr, 14,587 Mastery/hr, 33,781 Dust/hr. A 24h offline clamp pays 2,614,464 Gleam.

Facility upgrade cost is geometric while output is linear (Warren.cs:64-69, 118, 132-135): Gleam 5,300 * 1.50^level, Mastery 43 * 1.25^level, Dust 22 * 1.25^level. L1→L2 = 7,950 G; L10→L11 = 305,625; L15→L16 = 2,320,838; L18→L19 = 7,832,827; L20→L21 = 17,623,861. Nursery output over the same span goes 520 → 6,760 → 11,310 → 16,640/min. Cost grows 1.5^L, income ~L: the wall is exponential by construction.

Milestones: every 5 levels, +0.15 output multiplier per tier (Warren.cs:78, 81, 106-118). Warren XP: 100 per new facility level (Warren.cs:72), XpToNext = 1000*(Level+2) (Warren.cs:177), granting +3%/level All Production.

The full Hunter stat sheet — all 9 stats to the rank-60 cap, base 25 * 1.05^rank (HunterProgression.cs:17-19, 275-278) — costs 79,578 Gleam TOTAL. The un-upgraded Warren funds that in 43.8 minutes of doing nothing.

The entire Memory Dust prestige tree is 44 unlocks totalling 1,775 Dust (MemoryDust.cs:218-360). The un-upgraded Warren funds it in 3.2 minutes (via Game1.cs:393 and :543, `_dust.AwardFromMastery((int)w.Dust)`), directly contradicting MemoryDust.cs:96-98 which documents mastery milestones as 'the ONLY faucet'.

The entire Mastery build tree is 43 nodes (6 arms x 6 + 6 bridges + START, MasteryTree.cs:78-119), max 37 takeable because only one Mastery corner is allowed (MasteryTree.cs:209). Nodes cost 1 point each (MasteryTree.cs:177). Warren Mastery is added straight into Earned at Game1.cs:1274 — the un-upgraded Warren funds the whole tree in ~9 seconds.

Region farm auto-sell cap: 24 Gleam per hour (RegionAutomation.cs:33). Over the full 24h offline clamp that is 576 Gleam — 0.02% of what the Warren pays in the same window. The comment at RegionAutomation.cs:28-32 defends this cap as defusing an 'inflation bomb' of 760,000 Gleam per 100 hours; the Warren pays 10.9M in those same 100 hours, uncapped.

The cap is not actually per-hour: `_gleamCreditThisHour` accrues at 24/3600 per second and is never reset (RegionAutomation.cs:301-305). `_secondsIntoHour` (RegionAutomation.cs:71, 303) is written and never read — dead. Allowance banks without bound, so a farm left at stage 1 for 100h and then flipped to stage 3 instantly realizes 2,400 Gleam.

Idle efficiency bands, as % of par (EfficiencyContract.cs:43-50): NewlyConquered 25-40, PartiallyMastered 50-70, FullyMastered 80-100, OptimizedTeam 100-120. Interpolated by TeamQualityScore (EfficiencyContract.cs:65). Since every team is empty in the shipped build, TQS is always 0 and every region reads exactly its band minimum — the MAP's 'IDLE FARM: NEWLY CONQUERED · 25%' line (MapScreen.cs:303) is a constant.

Team Quality = 0.65 * CompositionCompleteness + 0.35 * (meanPowerTier / 20) (RegionAutomation.cs:20-21, 142, 155). CCS is filled/4 over four roles (RegionAutomation.cs:122-133). MaxTeamSize is 6 (RegionAutomation.cs:23) but AutomationScreen seats one creature per station across 4 stations (AutomationScreen.cs:112-118, 208-215), so the effective cap is 4. Hatches roll tier 1-3 (Creature.cs:163), so PQS starts at ~0.13 and the 0.35 weight contributes ~5 percentage points of efficiency — composition is worth 13x more than power.

Region mastery thresholds: 500 / 2,000 / 5,000 RMP (RegionAutomation.cs:13-15). Optimized additionally requires CCS = 1.0 (RegionAutomation.cs:169) — unreachable, because no team can be formed. RMP sources: 1 per healthy member work-tick (RegionAutomation.cs:10, 229-231) and 5 per active kill (RegionAutomation.cs:11, 186). With no team, the ONLY live RMP source is Game1.cs:1241 `_region.RecordActiveKill()` per champion wave — so 100 waves = Partially, 400 waves = Fully, and Optimized is impossible.
Work-tick cadences (Creature.cs:126-134): Crafter 8s, Attacker 15s, Support 15s, Defender 25s, Producer 40s. Never exercised in a real run.

Farm par clear times, derived at authoring time from health/dps + 2s overhead (EncounterSpawner.cs:36-46, SpawnTuning at EncounterTemplate.cs:54-61, averaged over standard templates at Regions.cs:158-162): verdant_hollow 17s, cinderworks 37s, umbral_reach 118s, marrow_wastes 270s, still_archive 645s, pale_choir 1,943s. At the 25% floor band, pale_choir is 7,772s (2.16h) per kill — 11 kills across the whole 24h offline cap. The DPS floor of 1.0 (EncounterTemplate.cs:56) clips in at tier 18, which is why the last region's par explodes 3x over the previous one.

Automation stages: 1 kills, 2 also collects cores, 3 also sells (RegionAutomation.cs:104-105, 276-280). The stage is a free `region.AutomationStage = Math.Min(3, ...)` on the +/- buttons and OemPlus key (AutomationScreen.cs:306-307, 329-330) — no cost, no gate, no unlock, despite the doc comment claiming 'Earned, not given'. Also unreachable.

Champion offline pay: `credited * save.ChampionGleamRate * 0.5` (Game1.cs:399), where the rate is a whole-session running average `_champGleamAccrued / _champSecondsAccrued` computed once past 10 seconds (Game1.cs:1256) and never reset. Uncapped except by the 24h clamp.

Champion live pay: `round(8 * HaulScale(wave) * mods.Haul)` (SoloExpedition.cs:190) with HaulScale = (1 + 0.35*wave) * (2.2 on boss waves) (WaveModel.cs:20, 26, 99-100). Cores only on boss waves, `round(2 * haul)` (SoloExpedition.cs:186). Threat compounds at 1.06^wave (WaveModel.cs:17) against linear reward, so the champion climbs to a wall wave, dies, and restarts from wave 1 after 1.6s (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:68, 265-267).
Region farm gleamPerKill is a hardcoded literal 8 at both call sites (Game1.cs:420 offline, Game1.cs:532 live) — not in any tuning record, violating the project's data-driven rule.

Offline clamp: 24 hours (SaveGame.cs:471). Negative elapsed (clock rollback) floors to 0 (SaveGame.cs:277). Autosave every 10s (Game1.cs:260, 985-990) plus on exit (Game1.cs:577-581), conquest (Game1.cs:1285), and every dirty screen edit.

Offline Warren runs with ConquestBonus = 0. `_warren.ConqueredRegions` is only assigned in TickFarms (Game1.cs:540) and DrawWarren (Game1.cs:558), both of which run after the offline tick at Game1.cs:391. A fully-conquered player's live Gleam multiplier is 1.62 but their offline multiplier is 1.02 — offline pays 63% of the advertised rate.

The welcome-back toast reports `champOffline + gleam` only (Game1.cs:435) and omits `wOffline.Gleam` entirely, even though that is the money that was actually credited two lines earlier at Game1.cs:392. A 24h return shows something like '+0 GLEAM · 0 KILLS · 0 CORES' while 2.6M Gleam silently lands.

Dust also doubles as a Warren upgrade cost, spent from the same prestige balance (Game1.cs:571, MemoryDust.cs:102-110), so the prestige tree and the facility economy draw from one pool — and the Warren refills it at 563/min.

Farm tick resolution: whole seconds live (Game1.cs:522-525), one big catch-up tick offline (Game1.cs:420). `_killProgress`, `_tickFraction` and `_gleamCreditThisHour` all carry fractions correctly (RegionAutomation.cs:67, 84, 246-252, 269-272) but none of them are in RegionFarmSave (SaveGame.cs:133-139), so all partial progress resets at every load.
systems.unlocks: Nothing gates the idle system: all 8 Warren facilities exist at level 1 from `new Warren()` (Game1.cs:150, Warren.cs:163-164) and the WARREN nav slot is open from the first frame (Game1.cs:1013, 1889). The champion starts fighting on boot and pays on every screen (Game1.cs:1026-1033). Downstream, the Warren gates essentially everything: it is the sole practical funder of the Hunter stat sheet (79,578 Gleam total), the Mastery build tree (Game1.cs:1274), and the Memory Dust prestige tree (Game1.cs:393, 543) — three separate progression systems all fed by one un-gated faucet. Conquering a region (7 waves, Game1.cs:1318) adds +10% Warren production and 40 Dust (Game1.cs:1280), and region mastery levels pay 15 Dust each (Game1.cs:1085) — but mastery now only advances via champion waves, so region conquest is a champion achievement, not an idle one. The region-farm system gates nothing and is gated by nothing, because it cannot be entered.
systems.depth: One real decision — "click UPGRADE on whichever Gleam facility is cheapest" — repeated until the 1.5^level cost curve outruns the linear income curve; the entire designed idle system (composition, roles, mastery ladder, automation stages) is unreachable dead code.
gaps: AutomationScreen.cs (544 lines: 4 role stations, hatchery, pen, feed/evolve, stage controls) has zero Update() or Draw() call sites. Game1.cs:1119-1125 explicitly no-ops it and Game1.cs:1516 routes the WARREN nav to DrawWarren() instead. Game1.cs:935 admits it: 'deprecated: the creature den was removed'.

Consequence: `region.Assign()` is only reachable from AutomationScreen.cs:214 and the save-restore path (Game1.cs:371, 379). A fresh game seeds 3 starter creatures (Game1.cs:468-473) but never assigns them, so `farm.Team.Count == 0` for every region and TickFarms skips every farm at Game1.cs:530 — forever. RegionAutomation.cs (315 lines) never executes past that guard in a real session.

Consequently dead in play: the CCS/PQS/TeamQuality composition math, all four idle-efficiency bands, the 500/2000/5000 mastery ladder as an idle mechanic, the 24 Gleam/hr auto-sell cap, per-creature work-tick accrual, and the AutomationStage 1/2/3 progression. All of it is green under tests (tests/unit/.../RegionAutomationTests.cs, tests/integration/.../FullLoopTests.cs:84-88) because the tests call the model directly, bypassing the missing UI.

Cores are produced (2 per boss wave, SoloExpedition.cs:186; 1 per farm kill, RegionAutomation.cs:277), accumulated in `_automation.Cores`, and persisted as UnhatchedCores (SaveGame.cs:39) — but Hatch() is only reachable from the dead screen (AutomationScreen.cs:224-233), and cores are not even shown in the currency pills (Game1.cs:1661-1668). A pure write-only counter.
Creature evolution is credited every wave and every chest (EvolutionCredit at Game1.cs:1248, 1263) against a roster the player can never see, expand, feed, or evolve.

The help screen still advertises the removed feature: Game1.cs:1787 reads ("A", "WARREN — HATCH"). WarrenScreen.cs:15-16 claims the creature den is 'preserved as a sub-view reached via the CREATURES button' — there is no such button anywhere in the file.

Offline Warren production omits the conquest bonus (`_warren.ConqueredRegions` never set before the tick at Game1.cs:391), so offline pays 63% of the rate the Warren screen displays for a fully-conquered player.

The welcome-back summary (Game1.cs:435) omits Warren offline earnings, i.e. it omits ~100% of the actual offline income. The HUNT screen's idle readout (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:774, `IdleGleamRate * 60`) has the same blind spot — it reports only the champion's rate.
`_secondsIntoHour` (RegionAutomation.cs:71) is written at :303 and never read — the 'per hour' cap is really an unbounded long-run average with unlimited carry-forward.
MemoryDust.cs:96-98 documents mastery milestones as 'the ONLY faucet' for Dust; the Warren's ForagingPits + SentryBurrows contradict it at 563 Dust/min via Game1.cs:393 and :543.
gleamPerKill: 8 is a hardcoded literal at two call sites (Game1.cs:420, 532) rather than a field on AutomationTuning, against the project's data-driven rule.

Partial idle progress (`_killProgress`, `_tickFraction`, `_gleamCreditThisHour`) is carefully carried across ticks but is not in RegionFarmSave (SaveGame.cs:133-139), so it is discarded on every load.

tensions.title: The Warren out-produces every other faucet by 3–4 orders of magnitude, so no currency is ever a constraint — including the one the trait tree will cost
tensions.detail: At level 1, before any upgrade, the eight facilities mint 1,780 Gleam/min, 240 Mastery/min and 558 Dust/min (Warren.cs:38-45, credited Game1.cs:541-543). The entire 1,775-Dust tree is affordable after ~3.2 minutes of idling; the entire 42-node mastery tree after ~10 seconds. Offline production runs at full rate capped at 24h (SaveGame.cs:471), so one night away yields ~270,000 Dust — 152x the whole tree. Every other faucet is a rounding error against this: conquest pays 40 Dust, a region-mastery level pays 15, a corruption deepening pays 60, and the region-farm auto-sell is hard-capped at 24 Gleam/hour across all six regions (RegionAutomation.cs:33) with a doc-comment claiming that cap 'defuses a genuine inflation bomb'. MemoryDust.cs:95-97 still asserts 'This is the ONLY faucet: Dust comes from mastering regions' and a test is literally named test_the_only_way_to_gain_dust_is_mastery — while ~99.9% of real income arrives from FORAGING PITS. Consequence for the redesign: converting prestige into a permanent trait tree does not make it a progression track, because it is not paced by anything the player does in the game. It is paced by wall-clock idle time on a system that started fully switched on. The flow redesign must decide, once, whether the trait tree is bought with idle-time currency or with play-depth currency — right now it is nominally the latter and actually the former, and the Warren also silently funds the mastery tree and its own upgrades from the same faucets.

tensions.title: Removing the reset makes the Dust tree and the Mastery tree the same object — three permanent trees already multiply the same five numbers
tensions.detail: MasteryTree and MemoryDustTree both terminate in the identical `BuildMods(Damage, Health, SkillRate, Haul, Rarity)` record (Build.cs:29-33), combined multiplicatively through the same `BuildMods.Combine` in `PlayerLoadout.ToBuild`. Gear traits and affixes feed the same five floats a third time. Composition: 36 of 42 spendable mastery nodes are flat +6%..+18% on those axes (MasteryTree.cs:80-119); 15 of 44 Dust nodes are flat +8%/+10% on the same axes, and every one of them is one of exactly five values (MemoryDust.cs:229,239,257,270,347). Today the two trees have exactly ONE structural difference: mastery respec is free, instant and unlimited (MasteryTree.cs:226-230) while Dust is permanent and unrefundable (MemoryDust.cs:126-133). That permanence was the entire justification for a separate currency, a separate screen, a separate node graph and a separate save field. Reframing prestige as 'a permanent trait tree' deletes the last distinguishing property and leaves two trees that grant the same mods, in the same magnitudes, in different currencies, on different screens, one of which you can undo. The redesign has to either merge them or give each a genuinely different verb — the honest split available is that mastery grants NUMBERS and the Dust tree grants VOCABULARY (keystones, Vows, triggers), which is roughly what the code half-does already and never commits to.

tensions.title: The prestige hole is not the reset (there was never one) — it is that the Dust tree was the game's only irreversible decision and its only content drip, and neither survives becoming a flat trait tree
tensions.detail: There is no prestige reset in the codebase: grep for Rebirth/Ascend/PrestigeReset/HardReset/WipeProgress returns zero hits, the DUST screen's 'RESET' button resets the category FILTER (PrestigeScreen.cs:206), and CorruptionScaling.cs:12-13 states the design pillar outright — 'a ONE-WAY ratchet that resets NOTHING (the game's prestige pillar)'. So removing the reset removes nothing mechanical. What the Dust tree WAS doing, and now needs a new home, is four separate jobs: (1) It is the sole gate on all build vocabulary — before vow_study_1 (15 Dust) the Vow axis literally does not exist (PlayerLoadout.CycleVow's option list is `[null]`), and each of the 13 keystones exists only behind its own 60-Dust gate. This is the game's only drip-feed of new verbs. (2) It is the ONLY unrefundable choice in the entire game. Mastery respec is free, the loadout is free to re-cycle, gear swaps are free, region travel is free, and death is free (a wipe mints a brand-new full-health champion at wave 1 with every wave's rewards already banked, SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:272-282). Strip the permanence and the game contains zero commitments — every choice is a toggle. (3) It is the only reason conquest, region mastery and corruption pay anything at all (Game1.cs:1280, 1085; CorruptionScaling.cs:32) — remove Dust's meaning and the whole world layer's reward column is empty. (4) It is the post-finish-line track corruption exists to feed ('so the permanent Memory Dust economy keeps moving'). Jobs (1) and (2) are precisely the ones a flat multiplier tree cannot carry: 31 of the 44 nodes are already an obviously-correct shopping list with no refusal in it.

tensions.title: Depth is quantized to multiples of 5 and gated almost entirely by one stat, so most investment produces literally zero observable progress
tensions.detail: Depth is the single number every system feeds and is scored on. But the boss multiplier of 2.2 is applied to enemy DAMAGE as well as health (SoloExpedition.cs:136 passes the same `scale` to both parameters; WaveModel.cs:25's comment only claims health), which makes every 5th wave a wall. Measured across a Python re-implementation of SoloBattle.ResolveWave: 20 of 21 sampled runs across the whole training range died on a boss wave. Depth therefore moves in steps of 5 and nothing else — stat ranks 21/24/27 all produce depth 44; ranks 45/48/51 all produce depth 64. Worse, at starter power the binding constraint is the 100 HP pool, not damage: 4x Projectile, 3x Projectile+Mark, 2 Projectile/1 Strike/1 Transformation, 4x Transformation and the starter build ALL reach exactly depth 19. So the two things the player spends the most time configuring — the loadout and the damage side of both trees — change the score by zero across enormous ranges, and the feedback arrives as a staircase with the risers hidden. Compounding it, `_regionProgression` makes a farmed region strictly harder (+35% HP / +20% damage per level, Game1.cs:1228-1229) with no combat-side compensation, so sustained farming can visibly LOSE the player a boss wall. Any flow redesign that keeps depth as the score has to unquantize it or stop scoring on it.

tensions.title: The mastery tree gives away for free the exact triggers the Dust keystones sell with a permanent tax — and the build screen can only ever wear three keystones anyway
tensions.detail: BuildTrigger is a shared vocabulary, held as a HashSet (Build.cs:307), so the same trigger from two sources is one trigger. Mastery notables grant them with `BuildMods.None` — zero cost (MasteryTree.cs:154). morph_n grants Echo ('EVERY SKILL FIRES TWICE') for 3 mastery points, which the game gives away by the dozen; the ECHO keystone sells the identical trigger for 60 Dust AND a permanent Damage x0.6 (Keystones.cs:61). strike_n grants Bloodlust free; the BLOODLUST keystone charges Health x0.75 (Keystones.cs:54). Socketing the keystone after taking the notable is a pure, silent, uncompensated penalty. And nothing gates breadth: `CanTake` blocks only a second Mastery corner (MasteryTree.cs:209), points exceed node count by mid-game, so every finished character carries all six notables — Bloodlust + Overdraw + Radiance + Desperation + Linger + Echo simultaneously — and the 'which arm are you' question the tree's own doc comment poses is never asked. On top of that, BuildScreen.cs:170 and :421 both loop `i < learned.Count && i < 3` with no scrolling, so only the first three keystones in catalog order are ever drawn or clickable: learn a fourth and it is permanently unreachable. The one genuine refusal in the whole build system — 3 sockets from a menu of 13, which Build.cs:204-222 argues at length is the point — is deleted by the UI.

tensions.title: Gleam's designed headline sink is unreachable, so all nine character stats are frozen and Hunter Level is permanently 1 while four screens display it as if it moves
tensions.detail: `Hunter.Train()` has zero player-facing call sites. The only calls in src/ are inside the RH_SHOT_MODE screenshot-fixture block (Game1.cs:761-775) and the save-restore replay (SaveGame.cs:447). StatsScreen.Update() is an empty method body (StatsScreen.cs:60) and the class doc admits it: 'stat TRAINING (hunter.Train) is intentionally not here — flagged for the owner, since it currently has no other home.' SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:260 says it 'moved to the CHARACTER screen (press C)'; CharacterScreen has no such panel. The help text still reads 'SPEND GLEAM ON COMMAND TO STRENGTHEN YOUR CHAMPION' (Game1.cs:1813) and the key legend still reads 'V — STATS — TRAIN' (Game1.cs:1783), pointing at a COMMAND screen that does not exist in the source. The stats themselves ARE wired to combat (SoloBattle.cs:136,157,159,161; HunterProgression.cs:233,238,263,269) — they are just pinned at base forever: AttackPower 10, Defense 0 (i.e. 0% mitigation from the stat), CriticalChance 5% giving a flat +3% expected skill damage for the life of the save. 79,556 Gleam of authored lifetime sink (HunterProgression.cs:324-328) vanished from the economy with no replacement, and ~12 unit tests still pass green over the dead feature. DamageBench — the live-sim instrument explicitly built 'so a stat that quietly reaches no formula shows up plainly' — was removed from the UI by the same commit and now has zero non-test call sites. The flow redesign must decide whether character stats come back or die properly; today they are a fifth power source that exists, is displayed, and cannot be touched.

tensions.title: Warren mastery and mastery-tree points are one variable with two spenders, and spending it in one place silently steals from the other
tensions.detail: `_mastery.SetEarned(3 + _deepestEver / 5 + _world.ConqueredIds.Count * 5 + (int)_warrenMasteryPool)` (Game1.cs:1274) folds the Warren's spendable balance directly into the build tree's derived point total, while `_warrenMasteryPool -= c.Mastery` on a facility upgrade (Game1.cs:570) spends the same pool. The Warren screen labels it 'MASTERY' (WarrenScreen.cs:66); the Build screen labels the identical number 'POINTS' (BuildScreen.cs:378); nothing in either UI indicates they are the same number. Two consequences: buying a facility silently removes build-tree points the player already counted on, and because `Available` clamps at 0 rather than un-taking nodes (MasteryTree.cs:178), the strictly-correct play is to buy the whole tree first and then dump the pool into facilities — you keep both. There is also a real precision hazard: `_warrenMasteryPool` is a long cast to int for SetEarned, and at high facility levels (~1.8M mastery/hr around L50) that overflows after roughly a thousand hours of accumulated idle time.

tensions.title: Rarity is a full build axis with a source and no sink, which makes several purchases strictly negative
tensions.detail: `BuildMods.Rarity` is one of the five axes the trait tree can grant. It is computed all the way through the sim, folded into `Haul.Quality` (SoloExpedition.cs:191) — and then nothing reads it. Game1.cs:1237-1239 credits only Haul.Gleam and Haul.Cores; DropBossChest rolls loot tier from region ladder / progression / depth / corruption and ignores Haul.Quality entirely; Chest.cs:184 derives quality from the chest's own rarity. Everything feeding that axis is therefore a pure cost: FORTUNE is -25% damage for nothing (Keystones.cs:113), DISCERNING EYE is -50% haul for nothing (Keystones.cs:74), the fortune_1/fortune_2 Dust nodes (45 Dust) buy nothing, SPLINTER's per-kill AddQuality(0.15) is discarded (SoloBattle.cs:188) which makes REAPER (-25% skill rate to grant Splinter) a pure downside, and SPLINTER is 1 of only 3 enchants in the entire WEAPON pool. The wiring test cannot catch this: DustEffects.WiredIds auto-passes any node that merely carries a Mods field (DustEffects.cs:194-200), so 'wired' means 'DustEffects reads it', not 'anything downstream consumes it'. One fifth of the trait tree's expressive vocabulary is inert, and three nodes (HUNTER'S LEDGER 20, FORGE INSIGHT 25, COMPLETE ATTUNEMENT 45) have no game-code consumer at all.

tensions.title: The only 'is this better?' number in the game is blind to most of what makes an item better, and it drives the auto-equip button
tensions.detail: `PowerRating = round(damageMult * attackPower * 2 + defense * 2 + maxHealth * 0.5)` (Gear.cs:113-114) reads exactly three things: the weapon's rarity/ilvl multiplier, the charm's Defense/HP, and Defense affixes. It never reads WornMods (every GearTrait — HEAVY, SWIFT, WILD, FOCUSED…), nor the Damage / Health / SkillRate / Haul / Crit affixes, nor any of the 11 enchants. So for Helm, Chest, Gloves, Boots, Ring and Focus — six of eight slots — PowerContribution is exactly 0 unless the item happened to roll a Defense affix, a 1-in-6 uniform draw. EQUIP BEST (CharacterScreen.cs:177-187), the green upgrade triangle (CharacterScreen.cs:339) and the Forge 'UP' badge (ForgeScreen.cs:1117-1119) all rank on it, so the game's own convenience button will actively downgrade a player who trusts it, discarding a Legendary with four damage affixes and an Overdraw enchant in favour of a Rare with one Defense roll. The same number is printed on the BUILD screen as 'BUILD POWER' (BuildScreen.cs:61,225), where skills, Vows, keystones and the entire mastery tree move it by exactly zero — the one number on the build screen is structurally blind to the build. A flow redesign that adds a fourth power source without fixing this adds a fourth thing the player cannot see the effect of.

tensions.title: Three difficulty tracks stack on the same enemies while the world itself is consumed in minutes, and the endgame ratchet is a free unlimited button
tensions.detail: Enemy strength is the product of three independent 'the world gets harder' tracks that no screen reconciles: the region ladder index (x1.35 HP / x1.25 dmg per step), region progression from farming (x1.35 HP / x1.20 dmg per level, Game1.cs:1228-1229), and the corruption tier (+60% HP per tier, CorruptionScaling.cs:18). Two of them are things the player does deliberately and one is a side effect of farming — and only the corruption track pays a scaled reward. Meanwhile the world layer they scale is tiny: conquest fires at wave 7 (Game1.cs:1318), which is one boss plus two trash waves, so all six regions fall in a few minutes of watching, after which the map's only remaining interaction is a DEEPEN button that is repeatable immediately, unlimited, free, and has no confirmation dialog (MapScreen.cs:104,310). Travelling to another region nulls the run and zeroes Deepest (SoloExpeditionScreen.cs:247-252), so the map's one real decision — stay or move — is priced as a total loss of your current depth against a loot-tier bump you cannot see. And the entire authored 'region mastery automation' half of the world layer (RMP work-ticks, the four-role composition puzzle, idle-efficiency bands, per-region farm teams, the 130-Dust SHARPENED RECALL line) is unreachable: AutomationScreen is constructed but never Update()d or Draw()n, so no creature is ever assigned, so TickFarms skips every region forever (Game1.cs:530). The world is simultaneously over-scaled and under-populated.
